Specific learning objectives: The Master's Degree Course in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies aims to train a professional figure with a solid cultural background and high levels of practical competence, who will be able to perform roles with responsibilities, in compliance with the areas of competence provided for by current regulations, in research, scientific innovation and the technical-productive development of biotechnologies applied in areas of interest to medicine, such as the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of human diseases, and in areas of interest to the pharmaceutical industry, such as the design, clinical testing, production and monitoring of drugs and biotechnological/diagnostic products at various stages of production/authorization for use.

The cultural, theoretical and practical profile of the graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies is also suitable for access to higher levels of university and specialist education. The learning objectives are achieved through an advanced training program, which includes a first common year and a second year structured in differentiated curricula: the degree course is structured on cultural and methodological aspects of disciplines characterizing the 'LM-9 class of Master's Degrees in medical, veterinary and pharmaceutical biotechnologies' (the functional areas for the specificity of the course are the following: Basic disciplines applied to biotechnologies; Morphology, function and pathology of cells and complex organisms; Common biotechnological disciplines; Laboratory medicine and diagnostics; Medical-surgical disciplines and human reproduction; Pharmaceutical disciplines) and is completed with knowledge and skills acquired in related and complementary training activities, which develop specialist aspects of some scientific sectors, even if not characterizing the LM-9 degree class, but consistent with the proposed objectives.

In particular, the learning objectives are achieved through an advanced training program which, in the first common year, will allow the graduate to:
- have knowledge of the fundamental and molecular, immunological, physiological mechanisms underlying human diseases, of congenital or acquired origin, and skills to design, develop and apply strategies for scientific development and innovation based on the qualitative/quantitative assessment of physiological and/or pathogenetic determinants of biological processes of human interest;
- have in-depth knowledge of the function and analysis of (macro)biological molecules and the cellular processes in which they are involved; knowledge and mastery of the use of biochemical-molecular technologies and bio-informatics methods/tools for the management and access to databases for an interdisciplinary and holistic approach to the study of complex biological systems and, through the management of DNA/protein engineering technologies and computational analysis technologies, for the development of scientific innovations that evaluate the dynamic interactions through which biological macromolecules produce functional properties in living organisms;
- have knowledge of the principles for the definition of epidemiological investigation designs and the ability to apply statistical methods in the biomedical field and in epidemiological studies in order to acquire the scientific method of investigation, the mastery of the principles of experimental design on biological systems and skills to organize and manage data from observational studies;
- have knowledge of the biotechnological methodologies applied to the biological and chemical-toxicological analysis of drugs, diagnostics, vaccines, chemotherapeutic agents and other biologically active molecules, and used for therapeutic purposes;
- have methodological knowledge and skills for the use of advanced biotechnological technologies for the study of the morphology and function of cells and/or cellular and subcellular structures (also in relation to their organization in organs, systems and organs) for the understanding, manipulation and dissection of complex biological mechanisms, through research and experimentation strategies, in compliance with the principles relating to bioethics, and based on more traditional systems (in vitro models) or on more complex systems (in vivo models), and to address specific biomedical issues, also for application purposes, in the medical and pharmaceutical fields.

The first year will also include the acquisition, within the scope of activities related to related and complementary disciplines, of knowledge and methodologies for the management and enhancement of intellectual property and projects resulting from scientific innovation.

In the second year, the degree course will be structured in differentiated courses (curricula) which, by deepening and integrating the professional aspects already acquired in the first year, provide more specific knowledge and skills for some application/employment areas of the graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies: the objective will be achieved both through some scientific-disciplinary sectors of the areas of the class, which already characterize the common path, but contribute to the specificity of the curriculum, and through areas of the class (in particular Laboratory Medicine and diagnostics, Medical-surgical disciplines and human reproduction and Pharmaceutical disciplines) to which a different weight is given according to the specific skills proposed in the curricula. The specialist nature of related and complementary activities can also contribute to the different curricular paths. In detail, in the second year the graduate acquires a solid cultural and methodological preparation through training courses that have a more diagnostic and/or more translational and/or more pharmaceutical character.

Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding The training program of the Master's Degree Course in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies is structured in activities that allow the graduate to acquire:
Knowledge and understanding
- of statistical and epidemiological methods applied to medical-experimental biotechnological sciences
- of the fundamental and pathogenetic mechanisms of human processes, of different origin, with particular regard to the identification of potential targets to be used in investigation and therapeutic strategies, in acquired and genetic diseases;
- of the biochemical and molecular biology methodologies, for the study/analysis/characterization of biomolecules/biological macromolecules and of the bioinformatic methodologies for the management of biological data present in databases;
- of the mechanisms underlying the interactions between drugs/toxins and biological systems and of the methodologies for biological and chemical-toxicological analysis for the therapeutic and toxicological evaluation of drugs and xenobiotics;
- of the principles that regulate the management and enhancement of innovation and intellectual property;
- of the principles and regulations underlying bioethics in the development of experimental protocols;
- of advanced biotechnological technologies and experimental models for the study of the morphology and function of cells and their organization in organs, systems and organs.

- interpret sources and scientific literature

The graduate in Medical and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies has:
- theoretical, scientific, methodological knowledge for the study of the morphology, function and pathology of cells of complex organisms, knowledge of the principles for the definition of investigation designs and mastery of technologies and principles of experimental design on biological systems, in order to design and develop experimental research, using in vitro and in vivo models, for the study of indicators of cellular and molecular pathogenetic alterations of diseases, congenital or acquired, for the development/monitoring of new biotechnological drugs and, in compliance with the areas of competence and in support of professionals also in the medical/clinical area, to participate in translational projects;
- advanced knowledge and ability to apply the principles of biochemistry, cellular biology, molecular biology and recombinant DNA for the management of both technologies applied to laboratory medicine and in the technical-productive field and of advanced technologies, for the development, validation and application of tools for investigation and treatment of alterations in the human organism;
- solid knowledge of the analysis and function of biological macromolecules and cellular processes in which they are involved and biochemical-pharmaceutical skills for the formulation and design, with advanced technologies and on chemical/biological/toxicological bases, of bioactive molecules, drugs, vaccines, xenobiotics;
- mastery of bio-informatics methodologies, for the organization/construction/access to databases, knowledge of advanced recombinant DNA technologies, proteomics and skills in pharmaceutical disciplines to collaborate, in concert with professional figures in the medical, statistical and chemical-pharmaceutical sector, in the development and validation of new personalized therapies based on the use of new molecular target drugs based on the screening of the most modern platforms and on technologies for profiling genes;
- knowledge of activities of pharmaceutical marketing and knowledge relating to the management of intellectual property/innovation projects, for the dissemination of scientific/technological information; to coordinate/participate in activities of development and consulting within the framework of programs for monitoring; to design and develop biotechnological products and proceed with their application in the industrial field collaborating/contributing also to projects for the enhancement and management of intellectual property in the area of biotechnologies;
- ability to learn autonomously and to understand and elaborate scientific literature in the sector, which supports the ability to operate in a professional context not only on standardized situations and models, but to guarantee a critical and motivated approach to the theoretical/practical/applicative choices made
- communicative and relational skills in the biotechnological-pharmaceutical area that allow to expand the comparison with the world of research and national/multinational companies, to relate to health professionals and/or specialists and non-specialists in the biomedical/pharmaceutical field and to disseminate scientific data.

- Biotechnology industries and service centers
- Pharmaceutical industry and control
- Diagnostic and pharmaceutical research and industry
- Biotech industry
- Companies for the development, marketing and management of biomedical equipment
- Bodies responsible for the preparation of health regulations and monitoring of clinical studies
- Scientific publishing companies;
- Scientific dissemination and information sectors.

Program, texts and objectives: Official language(s) of teaching and assessment: ITALIAN. Degree awarded: Master's Degree in LITERARY AND CULTURAL STUDIES. Specific learning objectives: The Master's Degree in Literary and Cultural Studies, in full accordance with the professional profiles and employment opportunities envisaged for its graduates, aims to provide the philological-literary, linguistic and historical tools that enable its students to achieve a thorough awareness of the complexity and problematic nature of texts, both literary and non-literary, which will be examined, analyzed and interpreted through the critical use of the bibliographic tools of the relevant field. Most of the disciplines are therefore in the literary, critical-literary, linguistic-philological area. Historical, philosophical, anthropological and geographical disciplines are added to complete the program.

Starting from a broad base of fundamental teachings in literary, philological and linguistic culture, and from the substantial coincidence of the methodologies applied, two curricula are proposed, focusing on the specific characteristics of the ancient world and the modern and contemporary eras, respectively. In particular, the classical curriculum gives priority to the area of learning related to the Greek and Roman philological and historical field, enhanced by teachings in the ancient, but also medieval and modern, literary and historical field; the modern curriculum is aimed at the knowledge and understanding of the Italian literary landscape and the evolution of the Italian language, placed in the broader context of Italian, European and extra-European historical and cultural development. The study plan concentrates most of the characterizing exams in the first year, and reserves the second year for the student's elective courses, thus allowing the possibility of dedicating a good part of their time to research and the writing of the thesis, for which 30 CFU are reserved.

Specific learning objectives:
The Master's Degree in Health and Nutrition Biology aims to train graduates with advanced and practical skills in the field of biomedical sciences and nutrition, combined with in-depth scientific and practical training in the disciplines that characterize the curriculum.

- solid knowledge of the properties of nutrients and non-nutrients contained in food and any related modifications during technological processes, the biochemical and physiological mechanisms of digestion, absorption, and metabolic processes related to nutrients, as well as the ability to assess, using the main laboratory techniques, the composition and body metabolism and energy expenditure, and to recognize the effects of quantitative and qualitative malnutrition.

Specific learning objectives: The Master's Degree in Chemical Sciences aims to integrate and strengthen the basic skills acquired in the first cycle in the various fields of chemistry in order to provide students with advanced training for carrying out activities aimed at scientific and technological innovation in the chemical field. The degree course also offers the possibility of acquiring specialized skills in specific areas of chemistry. In addition to the general training objectives of the class, the areas of specialization of the Master's Degree in Chemical Sciences, which will correspond to specific orientations or alternative curricula within the graduate's training program, aim to:
- provide advanced skills for understanding and predicting the reactivity of molecules and for designing complex syntheses. In this context, students will consolidate their skills in reaction mechanisms in order to develop the ability to understand, design and carry out syntheses of organic, inorganic and organometallic molecules.

Degree awarded: Master's Degree in COMPUTER SCIENCE. Specific learning objectives: The Master's Degree in Computer Science is characterized by significant independent project work by students, in order to develop their judgment and problem-solving skills. The skills provided by the Degree Course mainly concern distributed systems and mobile applications, computer networks, advanced algorithms, artificial intelligence, and the analysis and development of complex software systems. Through a constant analysis, the Course aims to incorporate but also anticipate the prevailing needs of the market. The Degree Course intends to introduce students to the most advanced and cutting-edge themes of Computer Science, both of a scientific and applicative nature. According to the vision of the Course, the Master's Degree in Computer Science is a candidate to be a protagonist of technological innovation in the international arena.

The Master's Degree Course in Environmental Biology and Ecosystem Management aims to train environmental biologists and environmental experts with advanced training in the field of environmental analysis, management, assessment and restoration, both in undisturbed conditions and in conditions altered by specific anthropogenic activities, climate change or unusual natural events.

The educational objectives of the course consist of acquiring: advanced levels of knowledge of the biotic and abiotic components of ecosystems as a tool for correct integrated analysis of the ecosystems themselves; ability to collect experimental data in the field and in the laboratory, with a critical approach and interpretative skills; ability to analyze data using statistical methods with the support of mathematical and computer tools, and ability to critically interpret the results; principles, methods and tools for assessing resources and environmental impacts, in compliance with current national and Community legislation; knowledge relating to the mitigation and compensation of anthropogenic impacts on biodiversity and the rehabilitation of habitats; autonomy in the implementation of new conceptual models and methodological protocols for field and laboratory investigations; ability to hold positions of responsibility in the management activities related to nature conservation and environmental quality control at national and international level; mastery of written and oral English, as well as Italian, with reference also to the disciplinary lexicons specific to the professional figures operating in the environmental sector; preparation of a high profile for access to Research Doctorate Schools and Second Level Master's Degrees.

The course of study provides for the possibility of choosing between two training paths. The first is mainly oriented towards the analysis of the various biological components of terrestrial ecosystems, including wetlands and inland waters. It is distinguished by the presence of a higher proportion of courses that deal with ecology and biomonitoring, even in sensitive habitats, and the effects of environmental impacts at different levels of biological organization. The second path is more oriented towards the analysis of phenomena at a more global ecosystem level and the management of the territory with a view to conservation and environmental restoration. It is distinguished by the presence of courses that deal with environmental botany, environmental assessment techniques, forecasting tools, territorial planning tools, bioremediation, and solid waste treatment. The two curricula provide for common courses relating to the physics and chemistry of the environment, earth sciences, the ecology of particular biocenoses, responses to environmental stresses, methods of biological conservation, and environmental economics. Professional status conferred by the degree:
The Master's graduate can carry out his/her functions as a freelancer or within public and private bodies that deal with territorial planning, environmental quality control (analysis of pollutants, terrestrial, aquatic and atmospheric biomonitoring), conservation of biodiversity, waste disposal, bioremediation. These include: bodies specifically responsible for the protection of the natural environment (Regional and National Parks and Reserves, WWF Oases, ARTA); Environment departments of public bodies (Ministries, Regions, Provinces and Municipalities) and private or state-owned companies (Municipal Environmental Services, Reclamation Consortia, Water and Wastewater Treatment Consortia, Optimal Territorial Areas). The scientific research sector also offers employment opportunities at Universities or research bodies/institutes (CNR, ENEA, etc.). Holding a Master's degree allows registration in the registers of the following professions, after passing the relevant State Exam and/or internship, where required: biologist, agronomist and forester, geologist, landscape architect.

The Master's Degree program in Applied Data Science trains professionals, the Applied Data Scientist, who can contribute within medium/large organizations as a key role in working groups that deal with framing analysis problems, planning and managing the acquisition of large data streams (i.e., "big data"), such as, for example, those related to market research or genome sequencing.

III - Autonomy of judgment
Graduates in Applied Data Science acquire a high capacity for reasoning and critical judgment that will allow them to identify the most appropriate models and techniques to manage and analyze data relating to the processes and activities of an organization in order to extract new knowledge and value. Applied Data Scientists have the ability to evaluate the impact of the proposed solutions in the application context, both with regard to the technical aspects and the organizational aspects. They are also able to identify and evaluate the broader and non-technical implications of Applied Data Science, such as those in the ethical, legal, economic and industrial fields. They acquire the ability to understand the limits of their own knowledge and are able to identify any methodological tools to supplement their skills.

Function in a work context. Function in a work context:
The Master's degree graduate in Applied Data Science holds high-level technical and/or managerial roles, as an Applied Data Scientist, Data Analyst and Data Manager and Data-Driven Decision Maker, as well as a support figure for specialists in data management, processing and analysis and modeling or technical figures in specific application fields. He can operate in contexts that require the use of computer, mathematical, statistical and data processing techniques in the tertiary sector and in public administrations, in the industrial and business sector, and in the scientific, technological and application sectors such as the biological and health sectors and the business sector. He is a professional figure to which are entrusted activities of collection, analysis, processing, interpretation, dissemination and visualization of quantitative or quantifiable data of the organization, for analytical, predictive or strategic purposes.

Specific learning objectives: Graduates of the Master's Degree Course in Infrastructure Engineering have a thorough understanding of the theoretical and scientific aspects of mathematics and other basic sciences and are able to use this knowledge to interpret and describe complex engineering problems. In this context, the professionals that this Degree Course aims to train apply existing knowledge in the field of design, construction and maintenance of complex transport systems, roads, railways, airports and ports, bridges, canals, dams and intake works, irrigation systems; they design solutions to prevent, control or remediate the negative impacts of human activity on the environment; they deal with the prevention and remediation of hydrogeological hazards and slope instability, and with the management of watersheds; they conduct research on the technological characteristics of specific materials and processes; they define and design standards and procedures to ensure the functionality and safety of infrastructure; they oversee and direct these activities.

- the planning, design, construction, management and monitoring of infrastructure systems;
- the technical assessment of the aspects related to the complex effects connected to the construction and/or refurbishment of infrastructure works;
- the resolution of complex problems related to the design and construction of infrastructure works;
- the analysis and evaluation of urban and territorial systems and the acquisition of planning techniques and tools at all scales;
- the assessment of risks associated with natural events, such as earthquakes, floods, landslides, in relation to the complex aspects concerning the design, planning, construction, refurbishment, management and monitoring of infrastructure. The achievement of these objectives is pursued through a training activity structured in teaching modules, which include classroom lectures, laboratory exercises and individual study or practice, and which lead to credits that the student obtains by passing exams.

The disciplines included in the training path are also organized chronologically in such a way as to allow first the completion of basic training in the field of Infrastructure Engineering, monitoring and the risks associated with it, and then to develop concepts and methods specific to the design, construction, management and monitoring of infrastructure and infrastructure systems.

The objective of the Master's Degree Course in Telecommunications Engineering: Advanced Technologies and Services is to train professionals with solid skills in Information Engineering and with specific preparation in one of the areas into which the vast disciplinary sector of telecommunications is divided.

Starting from a solid background in mathematical-physical and engineering disciplines, which is a prerequisite for admission to the course, the course goes on to explore the theoretical-scientific aspects related to the characterizing disciplinary sectors and aims to provide the knowledge and skills necessary to develop advanced design skills with reference to systems characterized by a high degree of complexity and requiring innovative solutions at the product and/or service level. In line with the evolution of recent years and taking into account the relevant professional fields, the course of study proposes a privileged educational path for the characterization, design and management of ICT infrastructures ("pervasive ICT infrastructures") that provide support for the most modern network applications (broadband services for users, industrial automation, automotive, advanced building systems such as smart buildings, power grid, etc.). In essence, the focus is on the network infrastructure, which is increasingly pervasive, articulated and heterogeneous, and which underlies the IoT (Internet-of-Things) paradigm and the world of networked systems and cyber-physical systems.

Assuming that students already have a good understanding of the basic topics of signals, systems and telecommunications networks, the curriculum provides for:
- courses in the disciplines that characterize Telecommunications Engineering, listed below: digital transmission systems, propagation models and modeling of communication channels, wireless communication systems, architectures and protocols for broadband and software-defined networks, photonic networks, signal processing and multimedia applications, systems for remote sensing, antenna systems and electromagnetic design techniques, design of metropolitan and access networks;
- courses in related or complementary engineering fields, such as: digital electronic systems, software engineering, embedded software architectures, stochastic models for networks and methods for controlling and optimizing network resources, models and methods for the environmental impact of radio systems, cyber security in the ICT field;
- specific in-depth study of basic disciplines, such as combinatorial mathematics, coding theory, algorithms for cryptography, operations research and optimization;
- further opportunities for students to choose training activities, which include strengthening knowledge of foreign languages, acquiring professional content, for which the degree program offers a structured offer, especially in the field of cyber security, and exploring aspects of business organization (individually or jointly combined with practical experience through internships in companies in Italy or abroad and in foreign universities).

The course of study is characterized by the combination of theoretical and methodological aspects relating to telecommunication systems with advanced skills in modern HW and SW technologies for the development and implementation of solutions. In this regard, it should be noted that the present course of study has already anticipated today's trends by introducing a module on embedded systems some time ago. The course of study includes project work and the explicit presence of an advanced laboratory teaching module with an adequate number of credits during the second year. Curricula have been defined with the general objective of intercepting a trend in the field of Telecommunications to differentiate in function of a greater focus on technological aspects and in general of a greater proximity of the topics to the physical level on the one hand and of a certain propensity to address the sector of networks and services enabled by these on the other.

The graduate in Telecommunications Engineering: Advanced Technologies and Services of the University of L'Aquila is characterized by the combination of i) knowledge of the most modern communication technologies and architectures and ii) skills in terms of ability to model, simulate, emulate and implement in the various operating environments, with particular reference to emerging technologies and new generation networks and services. Based on the acquired training, the professional profile for Master's graduates in Telecommunications Engineering: Advanced Technologies and Services allows them to carry out tasks related to advanced design, planning and management of complex systems and offers the basis for operating in the field of innovation and development of new solutions, basic and applied research for the development of technologies for Telecommunications, new generation networks and innovative services.

Specific learning objectives: The objective of the Master's Degree Course in Electronic Engineering is to train an Engineer capable of designing and developing advanced electronic technologies and systems, to be applied in various contexts. The characteristic that specifically distinguishes the learning objectives of this master's degree is to consider electronic systems in their complexity and entirety, also taking into account the issues related to the design and implementation of its components (both hardware and software). The Master's Degree in Electronic Engineering provides the necessary skills for this professional profile, deepening the themes of information and communication technologies.

Therefore, the graduate is able to apply the acquired knowledge for the analysis and design of systems for the acquisition and processing of information, which are determining elements in today's communication society. In particular, the autonomous re-elaboration of knowledge is delegated to personal deepening, in order to evaluate the degree of mastery of the knowledge acquired by the student, enabling him to find the appropriate technical solutions for the design, sizing and maintenance of information systems. The tests (written and oral exams, reports and seminar presentations of design works) involve the carrying out of specific tasks in which the student demonstrates the mastery of subjects, tools, methodologies and critical autonomy. The final test represents the culmination for the refinement and verification of the acquired skills, with the addition of any elements relating to innovation and research.

Specific learning objectives: The Master's Degree in Computer Engineering aims to create highly qualified professionals for the analysis, design, implementation and management of computer systems, applications and services based on the use of highly complex technologies, through the use of the most modern tools. Consequently, this course allows students to acquire a solid background capable of fully responding to the continuous demands for innovation that require a high degree of specialization and possibly an interdisciplinary approach. To appropriately pursue the specific learning objectives, the Course of Studies is structured into curricula that provide specific skills for the training of different professional figures, and which represent distinct declinations of a unitary project. Specifically, the unitary project provides for the provision of the following skills and abilities common to all curricula: analysis, design, implementation and management of computer systems, applications and services based on the use of highly complex technologies, based on the Internet and the Web, on robotics, and on artificial intelligence, through the use of the most modern tools.

Specific learning objectives: The Master's Degree in Management Engineering offered at the University of L'Aquila, in compliance with the learning objectives that characterize the relevant Degree Class, is characterized by specific learning objectives through a common section (including the majority of the credits provided for the characterizing and related/integrative educational activities) and 2 distinct educational curricula that allow for a specialized focus in terms of design of production and logistics systems in the first, and in the management of production, organizational and logistics systems in the second. The specific learning objectives and the description of the areas of in-depth study relating to the common section and the two identified curricula are described below.

With regard to the common section, it aims to achieve the following learning objectives:
a) to enable the analysis, interpretation and description of complex company problems based on an interdisciplinary perspective that provides for the sharing of approaches, tools and techniques from both the characterizing scientific-disciplinary sectors (Production and processing technologies, Mechanical industrial plants and Business and management engineering) and the related/integrative ones (Mechanical and thermal measurements, Information processing systems);
b) to identify and implement innovative technical, organizational and management solutions based on an interdisciplinary approach to the complex problems typical of Management Engineering, with particular focus on manufacturing companies;
c) to take into account - in the analysis, definition of alternatives, choice of the best option and its implementation - the contextual factors of a technological, sector, organizational and management nature;
d) to possess advanced knowledge in the field of analysis and evaluation of company costs as support for the decision-making process based on technical, technological, organizational and management variables;
e) to have adequate knowledge of production and logistics systems and production, organizational and logistics processes in order to allow further specialization in one of the proposed curricula.

The learning objectives of the common section are achieved through the combination of courses relating to the characterizing sectors and those relating to the related-integrative sectors. Specifically, with reference to the former (characterizing sectors), the topics relating to operations management and supply chain management are distributed between the first and second year of the master's degree course, while those relating to the evaluation of decision-making alternatives, based on advanced cost accounting systems, are concentrated in the second year. In the first year, an in-depth study of industrial quality management is also planned, in order to promote a more complete interdisciplinary vision. Finally, with regard to the related-integrative sectors, the focus is on the topics relating to the creation and management of databases and the management of industrial equipment.

Specific learning objectives: The Master's Degree in Chemical Engineering trains highly skilled technicians capable of tackling the design and development of process and scientific-technical innovation. The training builds on the basic engineering knowledge required for admission to the course and, in line with the relevant ministerial guidelines LM22 and the guidelines of the European Federation of Chemical Engineers (EFCE), is strongly characterized by the specific features of the location. The student is thus effectively involved in the process of transferring knowledge developed by research on key issues in modern chemical engineering. The training course is structured in teaching modules, with classroom lectures, laboratory exercises and individual and group study, with the assistance of the teaching staff. The student obtains the credits associated with the modules by passing the exams. The chronological structure of the training course, detailed in the table of training activities, assists the student in their cultural growth and gradually leads them to develop professional autonomy.

Degree awarded: Master's Degree in ELECTRICAL ENGINEERING. Specific learning objectives: The Master's Degree in Electrical Engineering aims to train technicians with a high-level university education and skills to develop and manage complex activities related to scientific and technological design and innovation and to promote research in a broad technical-scientific field. It aims to build, on the basic and engineering training required for admission to the course, a training focused on the in-depth study of the scientific disciplines specific to Electrical Engineering, without neglecting content from related or complementary cultural areas. The objectives of the training are the development of professional skills regarding:
- the design of systems and the management of processes related to the production, transformation, distribution and use of electrical energy;
- the design and control of electric machines and power converters, equipment and systems for electric mobility, industrial automation and home automation;
- the measurement and monitoring of electrical systems;
- the modeling and analysis of electromagnetic emission phenomena in electrical systems.

Function in a work context:
Function in a work context:
The professional figure of the mechanical engineer requires the technical-scientific knowledge, skills and competences necessary to interpret, describe, formulate and solve the complex problems that typically arise in an industrial context. Master's graduates in Mechanical Engineering acquire in the training course knowledge of the main characteristics of the methods, techniques, systems and most advanced tools used in the processes of the industry in general. These skills can also be expressed in freelance or employed activities within manufacturing or service companies, or in public administration. The degree prepares for the profession of engineer, section A, industrial sector, mechanical specialization.

The Master's Degree in Engineering of Control and Automation Systems aims to train professionals with extensive and solid skills in Information Engineering, through which they can understand, manage and contribute to the innovation of systems for automation, operating safely in national and international contexts. The Degree Course pursues the objectives characterizing the Class, training designers of automatic control systems and systems for industrial automation, for the energy transition and for electric mobility. To appropriately pursue the specific learning objectives, the Course of Studies will be structured in curricula that provide specific skills for the training of these designers and that represent distinct declinations of the unitary project.

The Master's Degree course in Mathematical Engineering meets this challenge and aims to train graduates with a broad multidisciplinary profile and characterized by solid theoretical-methodological preparation in mathematical modeling and scientific computing. The solid theoretical training will be accompanied and made concrete by knowledge and experience in at least one application domain, in the field of engineering or science, and integrated with the ability to communicate and interact with experts in areas of engineering, physics and natural sciences, economics and social sciences. Internships and thesis work in research laboratories and companies will constitute a further element of training, allowing students to put into practice the problem-solving skills and knowledge acquired.

The learning objectives of the study program are as follows:
- to be able to address complex problems in a multidisciplinary context in a flexible but rigorous manner, through the construction of mathematical models, and their numerical solution using computational resources for scientific computing;
- to be able to evaluate which solution techniques and computational and technological tools to use, developing an engineering approach aimed at solving a problem in the most efficient way possible;
- to be able to communicate and interact with experts in at least one application domain, understanding the main issues and the specific language. Graduates of the study program will have the training that will allow them to successfully enter the world of business, or to continue their studies in a doctoral program in modeling and computational fields.

The courses offered during the program are organized into various areas:
- Theoretical training: completion of basic mathematical and engineering training;
- Mathematical modeling, aimed at deriving, starting from the application problem, the mathematical model suitable for describing the phenomenon and analyzing the solutions from a qualitative and quantitative point of view;
- Numerical simulation, aimed at describing the methods of numerical approximation and integration and the methodologies for representing the numerical solution;
- Scientific computing: courses in this area will provide knowledge on the hardware and software technology of scientific computing, on advanced and parallel programming, on the management of large amounts of data, as well as knowledge of the design of efficient algorithms. - Applications: courses will be provided in various application areas, both introductory to the issues of the area, and on the application to this area of the methodological knowledge acquired.

The proposed "Mathematical Modelling" degree program (LM44 class) is international and inter-university in nature.
It stems from the ten-year experience of the Erasmus Mundus program "MathMods - Mathematical Modelling in Engineering: Theory, Numerics, Applications". This experience continues in the new Erasmus Mundus program "InterMaths - Interdisciplinary Mathematics" for the four-year period 2021-2024. In the version proposed starting from the academic year 2021-2022, the Master's degree is offered by the Consortium composed of:
- University of L'Aquila
- Vienna University of Technology (Austria)
- University of Hamburg (Germany)
- University of the Côte d'Azur (Nice, France)
- Autonomous University of Barcelona (Spain)
- Hamburg University of Technology (Germany)
The proposed degree program awards a joint degree. The duration of the program is the standard 120 credits over two years. The degree program is entirely taught in English.

The specific objective of the "Mathematical Modelling" Master's degree program is to train a type of engineer who is particularly skilled in the design, development and management of complex models and systems, understood both in the proper sense of Engineering (complex control systems) and in the sense of mathematical modeling (modeling, numerical simulation and optimization of complex systems). To this end, students are first provided with in-depth mathematical skills in areas such as mathematical analysis, numerical analysis, scientific computing, optimization and control theory. These skills are predominantly methodological and cover both the areas characterizing Mathematical, Physical and Computer Sciences and Engineering Sciences, the latter mainly in the disciplinary sectors ING-INF/04 Automatic Control and ING-INF/05 Information Processing Systems. Subsequently, the student will specialize in the use of various methodological approaches aimed at modeling, simulation and control of complex systems, also covering other characterizing sectors in both areas.

Dublin descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding Regarding mathematical theory and modeling, the student will acquire knowledge in the following areas:
- advanced ordinary differential equations, with particular regard to nonlinear dynamic systems and bifurcation theory;
- control theory, with particular attention to digital controls and more generally to applications in engineering automatic control;
- functional analysis and partial differential equations, in order to prepare for the study of complex models and systems. In addition, the student will acquire knowledge of the main numerical schemes used in the field of ordinary and partial differential equations. Finally, the student will deepen the knowledge base indicated above in methodological and application contexts consistent with the specific specialization chosen.

III - Autonomy of judgment At the end of the training course, graduates will have acquired a high level of advanced technical knowledge that can be applied to a wide range of professional contexts. This knowledge base is intrinsically interdisciplinary and versatile. It therefore allows to approach the solution of concrete problems by bringing a "new vision" to the problem itself. This aspect commonly manifests itself in the applications of mathematics to contexts of recent development, even not directly related to engineering applications, such as the modeling of "multi-agent" systems, which uses techniques originating from the study of gas kinetics. This example is paradigmatic of the potential impact of a mathematical modeler in an interdisciplinary research team, given his/her ability to "see" problems in an abstract way, decontextualized from their field of application.

In conclusion, the graduate in "Mathematical Modelling" is characterized by a strong independence of thought. At the same time, he/she contributes with his/her "mathematical" creativity to the understanding of the phenomena that "lie behind a problem", and to their solution through highly innovative and original techniques. In particular, the final test tests the student's ability to contextualize, in the most efficient and effective way possible, the various modeling approaches and numerical techniques learned to a problem never considered during the course of study, even coming from an application context different from the one considered in the courses attended.

Professional status conferred by the degree. Employment opportunities:
The professional profile and the employment opportunities expected for graduates in Structural and Construction Engineering are a direct result of consultation with stakeholders and the analysis of sector studies. The objective of the Degree Course is to train Structural and Construction Engineers who can practice the profession in the fields of Civil Engineering with reference to the design, planning, construction, refurbishment, management and monitoring of materials, structures and buildings, both in linear and non-linear fields, with particular attention to innovative structural and technological components and systems. It is consistent with the University's Strategic Plan 2020-2025, which, among its objectives, aims to promote the quality of the training offer with courses consistent with the needs of the individual and society. The profession can be classified, as indicated by ISTAT, in the category "Civil engineers and related professions".

Degree awarded: Master's Degree in Administration, Economics and Finance
Specific learning objectives:
The Master's Degree in Administration, Economics and Finance aims to provide a solid and in-depth knowledge of business and economic sciences in order to enable the graduate to fully understand the business phenomenon (also in the public sector) in its many aspects (economic, business, financial) and the fundamental economic dynamics. The Master's Degree provides a systematic ability to analyze the company, both in its structural dimension and in its functional dynamics, as well as the knowledge and methodologies necessary to carry out consulting activities in business administration and management, as well as the free professions in the economic and business area.

The Master's Degree in Psychology - class LM-51, qualifies students to practice as a Psychologist (as per articles 1 and 3 of Law 8 November 2021, n. 163). The Master's Degree in Clinical, Applied Psychology and Intervention aims to train professionals with a solid cultural base and high levels of practical competence, who can perform roles with responsibilities, in accordance with the current regulations, in the fields of clinical and neuropsychological psychology, in contexts such as public and private healthcare organizations, and organizations and institutions providing care and assistance to individuals. The Master's Degree in Clinical, Applied Psychology and Intervention also provides the theoretical and methodological knowledge necessary to design and conduct research activities, also in collaboration with other specialists, within the University and healthcare and scientific institutions. The cultural, theoretical and practical profile of the graduate in Clinical, Applied Psychology and Intervention is also suitable for access to higher levels of university and specialist education.

In particular, the learning objectives are achieved through an advanced course that includes training based on different areas of learning. These learning areas aim to acquire in-depth knowledge in the field of clinical and applied psychology in different contexts, in the methodological-statistical field and in the field of the psychobiological bases of cognition and behavior. The learning areas are developed by providing both transversal training between curricula and more specific training for each curriculum. To this end, the learning areas are structured differently, assigning different weights to the scientific-disciplinary sectors that characterize the course.

Graduates in Clinical, Applied Psychology and Intervention will possess in-depth knowledge of the psychobiological and functional bases of cognitive and emotional activity, and of the mechanisms and processes of normal and pathological cognitive and psycholinguistic development. In addition, they will possess advanced knowledge of the genesis and dynamics of alterations and disorders of cognitive, communicative, emotional activity and behavioral sphere. The master's graduates will also have targeted operational skills for the design, implementation and evaluation of diagnostic, rehabilitation and psychological support interventions in a clinical setting, and for the promotion of psychophysical well-being and health. They will possess skills related to the methodologies of psychological and psychotherapeutic intervention based on scientific evidence, according to different theoretical approaches. They will also be able to use the tools of psychological-clinical assessment (interview, systematic observation of behavior, use of tests) applied to the individual and group clinical process.

II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding: Graduates in Clinical, Applied Psychology and Intervention must demonstrate that they are able to apply the knowledge acquired in the design and implementation of interventions focused on the person or groups, also in interdisciplinary contexts, for the promotion of health as well as for the prevention, diagnosis, support and psychological and cognitive rehabilitation. They will be able to take charge, diagnose and direct to rehabilitation treatment individuals with cognitive alterations due to atypical development, a psychiatric disorder, a brain lesion or a cerebrovascular or degenerative disease. They will be able to operate in collaboration with other specialists within multidisciplinary teams, providing a specific contribution to the design and implementation of interventions focused on the person or groups. They will also have the ability to use the knowledge acquired to critically analyze the scientific literature in the specific areas of interest, design and carry out research in the field of clinical psychology, applied psychology and neuroscience.

Professional status conferred by the degree. Job opportunities:
Pursuant to articles 1 and 3 of Law 8 November 2021, n. 163, and in accordance with DIM n. 654 of 05/07/2022, the final examination for the award of the Master's Degree in Clinical, Applied Psychology and Intervention (LM-51 class) qualifies to practice as a Psychologist. The graduate in Clinical, Applied Psychology and Intervention will be able to use the knowledge and skills acquired in the training course in public and private healthcare organizations involved in the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of psychological distress (National Health Service, hospitals and clinics, territorial services, counseling centers, therapeutic communities, addiction services, residential homes, communities for minors, Prevention Departments, Public Health services, private third sector agencies such as cooperatives or volunteer associations), in organizations and institutions for care, rehabilitation and assistance to individuals, public and private. Further professional opportunities can be found in educational and school structures, in the University and in other institutions for scientific research.

 ITALIAN. Degree awarded: Master's Degree in DESIGN AND MANAGEMENT OF SOCIAL AND EDUCATIONAL SERVICES AND INTERVENTIONS.
Specific learning objectives: The chosen educational path focuses on the complexity of the interdisciplinary approach, not limiting itself to the usual disciplinary proximity between professional subjects and sociological and pedagogical subjects, but establishing, from the first year, the comparison on sociological and pedagogical subjects with a deliberately less theoretical approach, on the political science subjects, more attentive to local governments and intergovernmental relations. The common path of the first year includes, in fact, an in-depth study of pedagogical themes, through the provision of courses that allow the acquisition of educational research methodologies and an in-depth study of the themes of special education, as well as sociological themes, to which is added the study of the regulatory tools that govern the design in the social and educational sectors. The course is completed through the provision of optional courses that allow graduates of the class to deepen, alternatively, themes of a demo-ethno-anthropological nature or to acquire the fundamentals of financial management of companies.

In the second year, the course is structured around two educational curricula: the Specialist Social Worker (recognized in section A of the Register of Social Workers), and the Expert in the design of social policies. In addition to the ability to work with users who turn to social services, the professional who is intended to be trained must acquire the professional skills necessary for him to carry out functions of programming, organization and management of socio-health services, of direction of work groups and coordination of the services provided and the personnel employed in these services; he must acquire the necessary skills for a specialist use of cognitive strategies, communication, inter-individual relationship with professional interlocutors and with users, moreover he must develop his organizational skills in micro-systems, in the regulation of educational interventions and in the management of change. The curricular path also aims at increasing professional skills in research, monitoring, protection of health and the environment.

For this reason, the two curricular paths, although with different contents, provide for the acquisition of the management tools - which focus on the programming and evaluation of social services (Specialist Social Worker Curriculum) and on the management of training activities (Expert in the design of social policies Curriculum) -; of the organization of human resources and economic resources and which presupposes a common basis, which deepens the tools for planning and organization of social policies, a necessary prerequisite for social design. Furthermore, an in-depth study of some pedagogical themes is planned to allow graduates to acquire advanced tools for design in the field of inclusion and cooperation. The skills acquired and developed during the educational path can be used in the sectors of health, education, family, immigration, exclusion and social marginalization. And it is for these reasons that graduates of this course must possess advanced knowledge regarding the organization and functioning of social and educational services.

Hence the interdisciplinarity that characterizes the course and ensures that the knowledge that constitutes its core is acquired through the courses belonging to the sociological and social work, economic and statistical, legal and psycho-pedagogical disciplines. II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding: The master's degree graduate will acquire methodological, organizational and legal knowledge relating to the socio-health and educational services system, as well as knowledge of the most important forms of mental and social discomfort.

This Commission is made up of a minimum of three up to a maximum of five tenured professors. The Verification Test, lasting 60 minutes, includes thirty multiple-choice questions aimed at ascertaining an adequate level of text comprehension, knowledge of the morphological-syntactic structures and the vocabulary of the Italian language. Each correct answer will be awarded a score of 1 (ONE), while each unanswered or incorrect answer will be awarded a score of 0 (ZERO). The test will be considered passed if the student obtains a score of no less than 20/30. For the student who takes the Test and passes it, the Additional Training Obligations will be considered fulfilled.

nowledge and the additional training obligations to be fulfilled in the event of a negative outcome of the verification.
In particular:
1. The test for verifying the knowledge required for access to the degree course, pursuant to Article 6 of Decree 270/2004, is considered passed if the student obtains a score equal to or greater than the minimum set by the Board of the School of Economics, Business, Legal and Social Sciences. In the absence of an explicit decision, the minimum set in the previous year is considered adopted. 2. A negative outcome of the knowledge verification test results in the assignment of an additional training obligation (OFA), which consists of attending a remedial course offered on the knowledge required for access, held in the first semester. 3. Verification of the fulfillment of the OFA is carried out by passing a minimum of 18 CFU, related to courses provided in the first year of the study plan, within the scope of basic, characterizing and related subjects, by the extraordinary examination session of the first academic year. 4. In the event of failure to fulfill the OFA within the deadline referred to in paragraph 3 above, students must still fulfill the OFA and re-enroll in the first year of the course.

The ministerial provision also clarifies that any training debts must be recovered during the first year of the course. For the L11 degree program, the Verification Test of the knowledge required for access is mandatory for students enrolled in the first year. All students transferring from other universities and students enrolling in a second degree are exempt from the Test. The Verification Test is held according to a calendar indicated on the website of the Department of Languages, Literatures and Modern Cultures. Two sessions are scheduled: in September and in February. The Commission responsible for the Test is appointed by the Director of the Department. This Commission is made up of a minimum of three and a maximum of five permanent teachers. The Verification Test, lasting 60 minutes, consists of 30 multiple-choice questions aimed at ascertaining an adequate level of text comprehension, knowledge of the morphological-syntactic structures and vocabulary of the Italian language. Each correct answer is awarded a score of 1 (one), while each unanswered or incorrect answer is awarded a score of 0 (zero).

All students transferring from other universities and students enrolling in a second degree are exempt from the Test. The Verification Test will be held according to a calendar that will be published on the website of the Department of Languages, Literatures and Modern Cultures. The scheduled sessions are two: September and February. The Commission responsible for the Test is appointed by the Director of the Department, after consulting the President of the Degree Course. This Commission is made up of a minimum of three up to a maximum of five permanent teachers. The Verification Test, lasting 60 minutes, includes thirty multiple-choice questions aimed at ascertaining an adequate level of text comprehension, knowledge of the morphological-syntactic structures and the vocabulary of the Italian language. A score of 1 (ONE) will be assigned to each correct answer, while a score of 0 (ZERO) will be assigned for each unanswered or incorrect answer. The test will be considered passed if the student obtains a score of no less than 20/30. For the student who takes the Test and passes it, the Additional Training Obligations will be considered fulfilled.

In particular:
1. The test for verifying the knowledge required for access to the degree course, pursuant to Article 6 of Decree 270/2004, is considered passed if the student obtains a score equal to or greater than the minimum set by the Board of the School of Economics, Business, Legal and Social Sciences. In the absence of an explicit decision, the minimum set in the previous year is considered adopted. 2. A negative outcome of the knowledge verification test results in the assignment of an additional training obligation (OFA), which consists of attending a remedial course offered on the knowledge required for access, held in the first semester. 3. Verification of the fulfillment of the OFA is carried out by passing a minimum of 18 CFU, related to courses provided in the first year of the study plan, within the scope of basic, characterizing and related subjects, by the extraordinary examination session of the first academic year. 4. In the event of failure to fulfill the OFA within the deadline referred to in paragraph 3 above, students must still fulfill the OFA and re-enroll in the first year of the course.

In case of a negative outcome, the Commission will justify the non-admission, making the student's enrollment conditional on making up for the missing credits, by passing the relevant exams or, for linguistic deficiencies, obtaining adequate certification.

Remedial courses will be provided within the first year of the course to address any additional training requirements (OFA) in the subjects of Mathematics, Physics, Biology, and Chemistry, which are covered in the admission test, for candidates who score below a certain threshold. The methods and date of the admission test will be adequately announced on the University and Department websites (www.farmacia.unich.it).

Since this is a Laurea Magistrale course in English, another requirement for admission is knowledge of the English language at the B2 level. The B2 level is the fourth level of English (upper intermediate) established by the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR), a system for evaluating language proficiency at various levels determined by the European Council. Knowledge of the English language (B2 level) will be assessed through the entrance test and will be further improved during the course through the use of scientific English (reading and analysis of texts and scientific articles, use of technical jargon, etc.). For foreign students, adequate knowledge of the Italian language (at least B2 level of the CEFR) is also required for admission. Access to the Laurea Magistrale course is limited and regulated by law 264/99 and involves an entrance exam in English, prepared according to ministerial guidelines, aimed at verifying the personal preparation and skills acquired by the student in the fundamental areas of rehabilitation (physiotherapy, speech therapy, orthoptics and ophthalmology assistance, occupational therapy, etc.).

 Program, texts and objectives: Professional status conferred by the degree. Expert in food science and human nutrition.
The main employment opportunities for the professional figure of "Expert in food science and human nutrition" are represented by freelance and entrepreneurial activities in the field of Life Sciences (2.3.1.1.1 - Biologists and related professions). Graduates will be able to register with the register of nutritionists after passing the state exam. The agro-food, distribution and catering industries, as well as the pharmaceutical industries and analytical and market research companies, represent potential employment opportunities in the private sector. These are complemented by employment opportunities in the public sector: healthcare facilities, regional and provincial bodies, universities and research centers. Finally, access to doctoral courses and specialist schools also provides an opportunity for research activities (2.6.2.2.1 - Researchers and graduate technicians in biological sciences).

Communication skills will include knowledge of the English language in a way that allows him to confidently present his results in scientific settings such as international conferences.

The final exam for obtaining the master's degree consists of an examination on the discussion before a Commission of a written dissertation, prepared under the guidance of a supervisor, relating to a subject specific to the master's study path. The dissertation must demonstrate critical skills and the ability to address, with original results and with good experimental documentation, the themes of the degree class. In the preparation of the thesis, the student must use recent relevant scientific literature and the analytical techniques specific to the training path followed. The theses will be analyzed through the anti-plagiarism software Compilatio.

Knowledge required for access:
Pursuant to Article 6, paragraph 2, of D.M. 270/04, as this is a non-programmed study course, enrollment is subject to the possession of specific curricular requirements as well as the verification of adequate personal preparation. With reference to the curricular requirements, these are considered to be met if the student holds a three-year degree, in classes 17 or 28 (ex D.M. 509/1999) or L-18 or L-33 (ex D.M. 270/2004), or a four-year degree in Economics and Commerce (before D.M. 509/1999), obtained at the University of Foggia or at other universities, or other equivalent qualifications obtained abroad. If the three-year degree was obtained in other classes, the curricular requirements are considered to be met if the candidate demonstrates, with appropriate certification, that they have acquired in their university curriculum the minimum number of university training credits (CFU) indicated in the Didactic Regulations of the study course.

- be able to identify the tools and training paths suitable for the development of their specialist knowledge and professional skills;
- be able to independently conduct studies and research on the topics covered in the study path. Learning skills are acquired in the study path as a whole, with particular regard to the individual study provided, the preparation of individual projects, and the activities carried out for the preparation of the degree thesis.

Legal expert in security and personal data protection, corporate and labor. - Official within Ministries and, more generally, within the Public Administration with tasks of managing data security (legal department, privacy, ICT, etc.). - Legal consultant within corporate security. Corporate Security Manager. Data Protection Officer (more commonly known as DPO). - Legal expert in impact assessment and data management. - Official within the Authorities, with tasks of regulation in the sectors of communication and privacy. Legal consultant in the field of relations between Authorities, companies and public and private bodies. - Legal expert in the processing of data relating to workplace accidents and occupational diseases and the health data of workers. - Manager and member of the Prevention and Protection Service. Legal expert in analysis and design of workplace safety and environmental certification. - Legal expert in human resources management, with reference to new types of contracts (remote work, telework, flexible work, platform work and crowdworking) and related emerging risks. - Official in government security agencies.

The final exam (master's degree exam) consists of a public discussion, before a commission of teachers, of a written paper, prepared by the student based on original research of an experimental nature carried out at the University and at the bodies that hosted him during the internship or during the laboratory activities. The final exam, in fact, has the task of completing his training process, also of a practical type, allowing him to perfect his skills in terms of knowledge and to complete the acquisition of the ability to apply the knowledge already acquired within the internships or during the laboratory activities. The final exam will also allow the development of relational skills, communication skills and autonomy of judgment in the areas related to the legal, economic and technical aspects that relate to the field of security.

Knowledge required for access:
Admission to the Master's Degree Course in Legal Sciences of Security is subject to the possession of a degree (or a three-year university diploma) or other equivalent qualification obtained abroad. Pursuant to Article 6, paragraph 2, of D.M. 270/04, specific curricular requirements are required for access to the course of study, including the possession of a linguistic certification relating to knowledge of the English language at a level not lower than B2 (or passing an equivalent level exam), as well as the possession of adequate personal preparation. With regard to the curricular requirements, these are considered to be met if you have a degree in Legal Sciences (class L-14). If the degree was obtained in other classes, the curricular requirements will be ascertained, according to methods defined in the Course Study Regulations and on the basis of the documentation produced by the candidate, by a commission, appropriately appointed by the Department Council, which will identify paths within the Master's Degree depending on the curricular requirements met and/or the result of the verification of personal preparation.

Pedagogue
For graduates in the LM-85 and LM-50 classes, job opportunities fall within the areas of professional expertise of the 7th level of the European Qualifications Framework, as professionals at a senior level. Specifically, graduates in Educational Sciences and Educational Design work in the public, private, corporate, and non-profit sectors, in non-governmental organizations, in the field of cooperation and local, national, and international educational services, as well as self-employed professionals. As provided for in Article 594 of Law No. 205/2017, Official Gazette No. 302 of 29/12/2017, job opportunities relate to the various educational and training contexts, both in the socio-educational and socio-assistance sectors (limited to educational aspects), for people of all ages, in the areas of parenthood and family; cultural; judicial; environmental; sports and motor skills; integration and international cooperation.

The Master's Degree in Educational Sciences and Educational Design is obtained by passing the final exam (degree examination), which consists of the discussion of a degree thesis, with a high theoretical and/or experimental content, prepared by the student under the supervision of a lecturer. To be admitted to the degree examination, the student must:
- have passed the exams and obtained all the credits required by the study course
- have prepared the written paper that will be the subject of the final exam. The degree is awarded after a discussion of the paper before a specially appointed Commission consisting of lecturers from the University of Foggia. The final grade is awarded out of 110, with possible honors and mention. The characteristics of the final exam are regulated by a specific Departmental Regulation. Knowledge required for access.

To this end, the course aims to train individuals with technical and scientific skills in the field of construction and civil infrastructure and in the field of territorial management, which fully meets the needs of the public and private professional world. Due to the range of skills acquired, the civil engineer can find various job opportunities. design and structural engineering firms, construction companies, companies for monitoring and controlling structures, laboratories and research centers, and public and private bodies operating in the field of management of civil infrastructure and protection of the territory. Training objectives: The Master's Degree in Civil Engineering aims to train a conscious and critical professional, equipped with the necessary technical and scientific knowledge to design, build and manage complex structures, in accordance with the most innovative methodologies of civil engineering, and also to play a leading role in the field of territorial protection. A second objective is to provide training aimed at continuing studies in master's and doctoral programs. The training course includes laboratory activities and seminars and tutorials, as well as external activities such as training internships at companies and laboratories, and study stays at other Italian and European universities, also within the framework of international agreements.

Educational path: The didactic path, understood as the natural continuation of the three-year path and therefore following a solid basic physical and mathematical preparation, provides for the acquisition of knowledge and skills of a professional and operational type in all the characterizing disciplines of Civil Engineering, and in particular for:
i) the design, execution, management and control of civil construction works, hydraulic works, infrastructure, geotechnical works;
ii) the planning, design and management of interventions for the protection and development of the territory, and in particular for the planning of transport systems and for the management and protection of water resources, as well as the survey in the territorial and urban area;
iii) the evaluation, planning, design in the civil field for the purpose of safeguarding against seismic and hydro-geological risks. The course of study provides for four curricula, associated with different professional figures and employment opportunities:
1. Water and Environment
2. Transport Infrastructure
3. Structures and Seismic Protection
4. Sustainable Construction

These aspects will be addressed in particular through the disciplines of the characterizing SSDs, which will allow the student to confront engineering problems that involve a large-scale understanding of the interventions and, consequently, allow them to acquire the basic elements for a correct design and management approach. The master's graduate also acquires complementary and interdisciplinary knowledge, through the teachings in the SSDs identified as related, of the design and development of urban planning, the restoration and management of the architectural heritage.

The graduate in the Master's Degree in Civil Engineering has the skills to:

- address complex geotechnical problems, such as the design of foundations and support works, the analysis of slope stability and the implementation of consolidation techniques for the protection of the territory;

- design and manage hydraulic works (aqueducts, sewers, etc.) and works for the protection and safeguarding of the territory (works for regulation and defense against water);

Master's degree graduates in Science and Logistics of Maritime and Air Transport can access various maritime professions, including those in the offshore and recreational boating sectors. They can also participate in public competitions to find employment in public bodies (port system authorities, ministries, coast guard, European and international bodies) and research institutions, and can also work in shipping companies, transport, shipping and logistics companies. Graduates who have a sufficient number of credits in appropriate subject areas may, as provided by current legislation, participate in the entrance tests for training courses for secondary school teachers. Furthermore, the Master's degree graduate acquires the skills that will allow them, if interested, to successfully complete their professional training within subsequent specific training courses to acquire the skills for Category A and Category B hydrographers. For the purposes of admission to the Course, a B1 level of knowledge of the English language is required. Specific training objectives. The aim is to provide graduates with solid theoretical and practical training, characterized by a multidisciplinary approach that will enable them to address and solve problems related to the processes and management of activities connected to logistics and the maritime and air transport sector. The didactic structure is designed to enable students to acquire knowledge in the field of navigation, which will be gradually enriched by providing tools and opportunities for in-depth study, in order to acquire technical-specialistic and transversal skills, such as linguistic skills. The study course, structured over two years, provides for a common path in the first year and two orientations that students can choose in the second year. In the first year, the characterizing training activities are provided for the acquisition of knowledge and skills in the fields of navigation, logistics, remote sensing and oceanography, and the training activities present in the field of related disciplines for the acquisition of knowledge and skills on astronomy.

In the second year, the course develops through the provision of training activities in the characterizing disciplines for the acquisition of knowledge and skills required for the professions of offshore and recreational boating, and continues in the following two orientations:
a) naval, b) aeronautical. In orientation a) "naval", themes related to hydrography and maritime navigation safety are explored in depth. Particular emphasis is given to the skills for the training of a new professional figure: the expert hydrographer who acquires, processes and represents hydrographic data, through observations, sampling and monitoring of tides, currents and seabed morphology. The themes related to hydrography are developed in the training activities of the course and also in collaboration with experts from the Hydrographic Institute of Genoa through seminars, conferences, study visits. Hydraulic systems for navigation, such as navigation locks, are also analyzed, which require the use of appropriate methods and technologies to support the design, in order to limit the risk of system inoperability.
