The main employment and professional opportunities for graduates in Management Engineering are within small, medium and large companies in the manufacturing, automotive, energy, petrochemical and industrial sectors, and in the service sector, where qualified professionals are needed in the field of digitalization and sustainability. The reference organizations are:
- manufacturing companies
- food industries
- mechanical and electromechanical industries
- transport industries
- processing industries
- companies and organizations for the production and conversion of energy
- petrochemical industries
- public and private services
- public administration
- research institutions
- design firms
- consulting companies
- freelance activities (after obtaining state exam certification). Characteristics of the final exam. The final exam for obtaining the Master's Degree consists of a public discussion of the thesis, relating to an original work carried out by the student. The thesis should preferably be of an applied, design or experimental nature, from which the Commission can evaluate the cultural and scientific maturity as well as the quality of the work carried out.

The Master's Degree Course (CdSM) in Management Engineering (LM-31 class) aims to train Management Engineers capable of managing and optimizing the various areas/functions of public and private companies, through the application of technical-managerial approaches, capable of finding solutions to interdisciplinary problems related to the organization and management of processes and projects and of adopting innovative systems, effectively responding to current market needs and its rapid changes, in particular those related to digitalization and sustainability. The specific training objectives of the CdSM, consistent with the training objectives that characterize the LM-31 degree class, contribute to acquiring knowledge and skills summarized in the following three areas of learning:
- area of management of production systems and projects: theoretical-scientific aspects of the management and optimization of processes and production systems including project management techniques and industrial risk analysis to identify, address and solve complex and interdisciplinary problems also concerning the broader concept of supply chain in the field of production/delivery of goods and services.

The Master's Degree Course (CdSM) in Bioengineering (class LM-21) aims to train biomedical engineers, with solid methodological foundations and with high professional qualifications, capable of designing and developing products and systems in the area of Bioengineering in general, and with particular reference to solutions and technologies aimed at supporting the complex challenges related to the human brain and the nervous system. In this way, students will develop an interdisciplinary cultural training, closely linked on the one hand to the sectors of Information Engineering and Industrial Engineering, and on the other to the medical-biological and legal-regulatory sectors, which constitute the natural field of application and employment, represented by public and private actors and stakeholders.

Acquire knowledge and develop skills related to the functioning of the nervous system, its pathological alterations, and the technologies for monitoring and intervention, including medical imaging diagnostics.

Characteristics of the final exam. The final exam consists of the preparation, under the supervision of a lecturer, of an original written paper on topics related to one of the courses taken by the student during his/her master's degree program. To pass the final exam, the student must demonstrate that he/she has acquired, in addition to an advanced knowledge of the chosen topic, also an autonomous ability to learn, understand and research; the ability to correctly use the literature (including international literature); the ability to manage, analyze and present data; the ability to expose and support scientific arguments in a logical and coherent way, demonstrating maturity in the analysis, synthesis and organization of the topics covered. - apply the principles of economic theory to real case studies
- analyze the effects of the decisions of economic operators
- evaluate the impact of the direct and indirect effects generated by the activities of a company or a public administration

- assicurare, mediante appositi insegnamenti o, all'interno di insegnamenti già esistenti, l'acquisizione di adeguate conoscenze: a) degli aspetti istituzionali ed organizzativi degli ordinamenti giudiziari; b) della deontologia professionale, della logica ed argomentazione giuridica e forense, della sociologia giuridica, dell'informatica giuridica; c) del linguaggio giuridico di almeno una lingua straniera (inglese).

E' anche richiesta la capacità di evidenziare divergenze e analogie tra diversi sistemi giuridici. E' necessaria anche la capacità di inquadrare gli istituti volti a disciplinare il rapporto fra cittadino e pubblica amministrazione per la tutela di interessi legittimi e interessi diffusi. NOTAIO Lo Stato demanda al notaio due principali compiti: attribuire pubblica fede agli atti e procedere alla riscossione delle imposte per attività ed operazioni economicamente rilevanti. Deve accertare personalmente qual è la volontà delle persone che a lui si rivolgono e lo scopo da raggiungere, al fine di predisporre l'atto, conforme alla legge, più idoneo ed economico. A tal fine è imprescindibile l'attività di consulenza del notaio prima della stipula dell'atto. Svolge, quindi, una funzione di controllo preventivo di legalità.

Esperto legale per l'innovazione L'esperto legale per l’innovazione potrà ricoprire ruoli apicali di direzione e coordinamento, nella pubblica amministrazione o nell’impresa, operando in ambiti di responsabilità che richiedono padronanza delle nuove tecnologie applicate al diritto e degli effetti giuridici della svolta digitale sulla responsabilità delle imprese e della pubblica amministrazione. Il laureato potrà operare come Manager nel settore pubblico o privato, in qualità di esperto della gestione dei processi di innovazione digitale come pure della gestione del rischio derivante da tali processi. La figura professionale formata potrà operare anche come consulente esterno (advisor) per la regolazione delle complessità organizzative e di compliance; ambire ad una carriera di top executive o di legal entrepreneur a livello interno ed internazionale, o creare imprese innovative in settori necessitanti la riscrittura delle regole tradizionali per conformarsi alla svolta digitale.

Professional status conferred by the degree. The LM course offers various professional opportunities in public administrations, local authorities and public and private service structures. In particular, sociologists trained in LM-88 will be able to hold positions as officials or managers in public, private and social private organizations. Research, consulting and training roles. They will also be able to carry out specialist consulting functions in social research, as organization analysts, as public policy analysts, as experts in human resource management. They will hold managerial roles in structures dedicated to the study or implementation of social policies (services for families, children, the elderly, drug addicts, the mentally ill, etc.); in the field of training, guidance and information. On the other hand, specialist social workers trained in LM-87 will find employment with functions of design or coordination in public and private structures that manage social services; in structures that provide services to people (Local Health Authorities, Ministry of Labor, Health, Social Policies, Equal Opportunities, Justice, Interior).

Graduates of the LM-87 class can, after passing the state exam, access the register of specialist social workers (section A). All graduates of the course can continue their studies in second-level master's degrees with a sociological and psychological or social work focus, as well as in research doctorate courses activated in the specific area. Characteristics of the final exam. The final exam will consist of a discussion of a written paper, with requirements of originality, on a topic of relevance for the graduate's training project, of which it is an integral part. The paper will be agreed upon with one or more teachers and must present the results of a research work developed independently, albeit under the supervision of a teacher of the course. The treatment must demonstrate knowledge of the main and most up-to-date reference literature as well as the methodological tools required by research in the field. The exam will be a significant moment in the graduate's training and will play a fundamental role in completing their learning path. In this perspective, it can also be developed in connection with the planned internship and training activities.

- an advanced capacity for analysis and interpretation of social phenomena;
- an in-depth knowledge of the economic, historical and political framework in relation to specific areas of applied sociological analysis, of reading the needs of the territory and of designing social interventions;
- a high knowledge of the methods and techniques of social research and social work;
- an adequate methodological, organizational and legal knowledge relating to the system of socio-health services;
Knowledge and understanding skills of the indicated topics will be acquired through:
- participation in lectures, exercises, seminars
- personal study, guided and autonomous, within the scope of the training activities. II - Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.

Graduates will be able to:
- design, carry out and coordinate research in sociology and social intervention. - apply theoretical knowledge to the analysis of social functioning;
- apply advanced methodological skills relating to the collection and processing of data relevant to social research to concrete cases;
- operate in interdisciplinary contexts, participating in complex design and working groups;

- understand social changes by identifying emerging problems and designing social policy interventions. - analyze data and information in numerical or textual form. - operate in evaluation and design in the fields of social sciences and social services. The training course that characterizes the Master's Degree Course in Veterinary Biotechnology aims to build professional figures with multidisciplinary skills in the biotechnological field. The course aims to train professionals who are able to understand the phenomena that underlie biotechnological processes, intervening ad hoc through the application of new methodological principles. The first year of the course includes specialist compulsory courses common to all students, which allow them to acquire basic and advanced knowledge in the field of veterinary biotechnology, relating to the morpho-functional and animal biomolecular learning area, which allow them to achieve in-depth theoretical and practical training on biotechnological methodologies in the cellular and molecular field, which represent the essential cultural baggage underlying the professional activity required by the market.

The final exam consists of the preparation and discussion, before a Commission appointed according to the Faculty's didactic regulations, of a dissertation in which the student demonstrates that they have acquired a rigorous research method in a specific area of educational sciences (and with a specific declination: theoretical, historical or empirical) and that they have developed adequate argumentative skills. This exam will take place in a public session before a commission of teachers, who will express the overall evaluation in hundredths. The final degree grade will be determined by the average of the grades obtained in the individual profit exams, the quality of the credits acquired and the discussion of the final paper produced by the student. The activities related to the preparation of the final exam for the achievement of the degree will be carried out by the student under the supervision of a teacher. The paper may also be written in a foreign language previously studied. Knowledge required for admission. Graduates in the Master's Degree courses of this class, upon completion and refinement of the training acquired in the three-year degree courses of class 18, must possess:

• good mastery of the main IT tools and telematics communication in the specific areas of competence;
• fluent possession, in writing and orally, of at least one language of the European Union, in addition to Italian, with reference also to disciplinary lexicons.

At the end of the course, the student must demonstrate that they have consolidated the theoretical knowledge specifically relating to the sciences of education (pedagogy, philosophy, psychology, sociology, etc.) already acquired in the first university cycle. This must guarantee the student:
- the ability to analyze, understand and effectively manage the different training contexts and the problems connected to them;
- adequate skills and abilities to solve problems in operational and/or research contexts that are broader, more complex or, in general, unusual but still connected to the specific sector of study/educational/training intervention. The knowledge must concern in particular:
- the epistemological structure of the individual disciplines that make up the sciences of education;
- the interdisciplinary relationships that connect them;
- the didactics relating to the same disciplines. The level of competence acquired is evaluated during the course through oral interviews and/or written tests and/or papers on specific disciplinary topics.

This complexity derives above all from the heterogeneity of the issues they will be confronted with, which is why strong capacities of autonomy and responsibility of judgement are required, which are correlated above all by the study of disciplines with a high theoretical and reflexive content, such as philosophical knowledge, communication practices, research methodologies and theories of language.

Dublin Descriptors: I - Knowledge and understanding: Graduates refine and deepen the linguistic, literary, historical and archaeological knowledge relating to the ancient and medieval world already acquired during the three-year degree, in order to know, understand and interpret correctly the literary, historical and archaeological phenomena relating to those cultures. As regards the field of literary disciplines, one moves from simple texts to more complex texts with the aid of critical editions; from simple metric structures (e.g. hexameter, trimeter iambic) to complex structures such as lyrical meter. As regards historical phenomena, from a general knowledge of events and their interpretation, one moves on to monographic studies that allow the acquisition of more refined methodologies of investigation on the political, institutional, social and economic problems of the Greek and Roman world. All this with the contribution of technical disciplines such as philology and rhetoric, papyrology, epigraphy. In the field of archaeological disciplines, graduates know in detail the development of ancient and medieval archaeology, with particular reference to Sicily and southern Italy.

The Master's Degree Course in BIOLOGY AND ECOLOGY OF THE COASTAL MARINE ENVIRONMENT aims to train professionals in the field of biology and ecology of the coastal marine environment with specific skills and design capabilities in the monitoring, management and protection, from a biological and ecological point of view, of coastal marine environments, including brackish and transition environments, as well as in the management of aquaculture plants, aquariums, marine parks and protected areas. The Master's Degree Course in Physics aims to train graduates with solid knowledge in the characterizing areas in order to achieve that flexible but rigorous mindset that allows direct access to work activities that require in-depth knowledge of the main physical theories and the scientific method and a predisposition to rapid learning of innovative methodologies and technologies, even in an interdisciplinary field. The Master's degree graduate in Physics must be able to use his level of specialization in the application phase of his skills and in the ability to update his knowledge. The Master's Degree in Physics is also positioned as an intermediate stage in a training aimed at training for scientific research activities that take place in doctoral courses, providing the student with the skills to face basic and applied scientific research paths as well as the ability to design and develop physical methodologies appropriate for the different problems. The training offer is structured in four semesters in which advanced and specialized knowledge is acquired in the field of Theoretical Physics, Modern Physics and Experimental Physics.

a) develop an adequate set of skills and approaches oriented to Problem Solving through the techniques and methodologies learned to formulate, even in an innovative way, qualitative and quantitative answers to complex problems involving the processing and analysis of data;
b) provide multidisciplinary training that includes both specific technical-scientific knowledge and knowledge of the business, legal and/or social context in the field of data processing and analysis;
c) deepen the principles of the Data Economy, Data-driven Business and Business Intelligence to analyze complex macro and micro-economic phenomena that influence political, economic and social decisions and business strategies;
d) provide basic knowledge to combine mathematical-statistical and computer technologies and methodologies with specific methods and techniques to adapt them to the reference application context;
e) develop the ability to effectively support change and technological and organizational innovation in companies and public and private bodies, in particular in the aspects involving the use and processing of large amounts of data, taking into account constraints related to security and privacy;
f) train a new generation of scientific and cultural profiles that respond to the emerging needs of Digital Transformation of all organizations, public and private, that aspire to high competitiveness in their reference sector and in a globalized context.

a) a preparation that includes both specific technical knowledge and knowledge of the business, legal and/or social context;
b) knowledge of mathematical-statistical and computer technologies and methodologies with specific methods and techniques of the area in which they will operate;
c) understanding of the scientific methodology for the processing of large data sets. The methods and tools used to achieve and verify the expected results include the profit exams, which can be oral and/or written and/or practical, and take place at the end of each training activity, according to methods established by the individual teachers.

Data Architect: The Data Architect designs the information flows within business processes, identifying the reference requirements for the design of company information systems. He/She uses the technical skills on computer languages oriented to data to plan architectural strategies for each thematic area of the business model. Data Scientist: The work of the Data Scientist consists in extracting valuable information for the various business needs: business, marketing and sales strategies, definition of new products and services, etc. This professional develops and implements mathematical-statistical models to be applied on Big Data in order to try to answer complex questions related to the specific application and analysis domain. Market Analyst: The Market Analyst is able to carry out the analysis of economic/business problems using methods for managing large amounts of data. THE FIRST-LEVEL UNIVERSITY MASTER'S DEGREE PROGRAM ENTITLED "SUPERVISION FOR SOCIAL SERVICES (SUPISS)"
AIMS TO TRAIN SUPERVISORS IN THE FIELD OF SOCIAL AND SOCIO-HEALTH SERVICES, COMPETENT IN PROMOTING THE HIGH QUALITY OF SERVICES, OFFERING ADEQUATE RESPONSES TO CITIZENS' NEEDS, AND SUPPORTING THE WELL-BEING OF PROFESSIONALS. TO THIS END, THE COURSE WILL AIM TO IDENTIFY SUPERVISION PATHS DESIGNED TO CONSOLIDATE EXISTING SKILLS AND ACQUIRE NEW ONES; ENHANCE THE SKILLS, ABILITIES, ATTITUDES, AND PERSONAL CHARACTERISTICS OF SOCIAL WORKERS AND SOCIAL WORKERS IN THE FIELD; FOSTER GREATER AWARENESS OF THE RISKS AND OPPORTUNITIES AND THE WAYS TO ADDRESS THEM IN PROFESSIONAL WORK;
DEVELOP GREATER CAPACITY FOR SOCIAL WORKERS TO ACT THROUGH COORDINATED AND INTEGRATED ACTIONS WITH OTHER ACTORS IN THE ORGANIZATIONAL AND SOCIAL CONTEXT IN WHICH THEY OPERATE;
PROVIDE TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES TO IMPLEMENT THESE ACTION COURSES; INCREASE THEIR CAPACITY FOR REFLECTION IN ORDER TO CORRECT OR IDENTIFY MORE APPROPRIATE AND FEASIBLE PATHS WITH RESPECT TO THE NEEDS OF THE USERS.

IN PARTICULAR, COMPUTER SCIENCE MASTER'S DEGREE GRADUATES MUST: - POSSESS SOLID KNOWLEDGE OF BOTH THE FOUNDATIONS AND THE APPLICATION ASPECTS OF THE VARIOUS SECTORS OF COMPUTER SCIENCE; - HAVE A THOROUGH UNDERSTANDING OF THE PRINCIPLES, STRUCTURES, AND USE OF PROCESSING SYSTEMS; - KNOW THE FUNDAMENTALS, TECHNIQUES, AND METHODS OF DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF COMPUTER SYSTEMS, BOTH BASIC AND APPLICATION-ORIENTED; - HAVE KNOWLEDGE OF DIFFERENT APPLICATION SECTORS; - BE ABLE TO WORK WITH A HIGH DEGREE OF AUTONOMY, WITH GOOD DIRECTIVE, COMMUNICATION, AND MANAGERIAL SKILLS IN LEADING WORK GROUPS. THESE SKILLS ARE ACQUIRED THROUGH LECTURES AND LABORATORY EXERCISES, INDEPENDENT AND GROUP PROJECT ACTIVITIES, AND THESIS WORK. Level of satisfaction of graduates and employment status of graduates: GRADUATE PROFILE AND RELEVANT EMPLOYMENT STATUS.

ORTA, Course Director: AMALIA PORTA. Characteristics and other information: Professional status conferred by the degree.
THE MASTER'S IN "MICROBIOLOGICAL CONTROLS: QUALITY AND SAFETY IN PRODUCTION PROCESSES" AIMS TO TRAIN EXPERTS IN THE MANAGEMENT OF SAFETY AND QUALITY CONTROL PROCESSES IN VARIOUS OCCUPATIONAL FIELDS, SUCH AS:
- FOOD INDUSTRIES,
- PHARMACEUTICAL INDUSTRIES;
- COSMETIC INDUSTRIES;
- PUBLIC AND PRIVATE LABORATORIES OF APPLIED BIOTECHNOLOGY. Specific learning objectives:
THE AIM IS TO PROVIDE THEORETICAL/PRACTICAL TRAINING THAT ACCOMPANIES PARTICIPANTS TOWARDS THE ACQUISITION OF A BROAD AND INNOVATIVE PROFESSIONAL SKILL IN MICROBIOLOGICAL QUALITY CONTROL, THROUGH THE ABILITY TO ADOPT AND EMPLOY UP-TO-DATE AND VALID MICROBIOLOGICAL ANALYSIS METHODS AND TECHNIQUES, AS PROVIDED FOR BY NATIONAL AND EUROPEAN REGULATIONS, WITH PARTICULAR REFERENCE TO THE GUIDELINES OF THE "EUROPEAN PHARMACOPOEIA" AND THE "CLINICAL AND LABORATORY STANDARDS INSTITUTE (C.L.S.I.)".

qualification Roles Course Coordinator MASSIMO AMATO Characteristics and Other Information Specific learning objectives.
THE ANNUAL UNIVERSITY ADVANCED TRAINING COURSE ENTITLED DIGITAL WORKFLOWS AND INNOVATIVE TECHNIQUES IN IMPLANT AND RECONSTRUCTIVE SURGERY IS A THEORETICAL AND PRACTICAL COURSE AIMED AT TRAINING "PROFESSIONALS SKILLED IN THE FIELD OF MODERN DIGITAL IMPLANTOPROSTHETIC AND REGENERATIVE SURGERY OF HARD AND SOFT TISSUES". THE COURSE AIMS TO ENHANCE THE BASIC KNOWLEDGE AND PRACTICAL SKILLS OF STUDENTS, PROVIDING IN-DEPTH INFORMATION ON THE DIAGNOSTIC PATHWAYS LEADING TO THE MANAGEMENT OF PERI-IMPLANTOPROSTHETIC TREATMENT PROTOCOLS.

DENTED AND INNOVATIVE MIX OF ACADEMIC KNOWLEDGE, AS DEMONSTRATED BY THE TWO CURRICULA THAT DEFINE THE EDUCATIONAL OFFER.
THE CURRICULUM IN DIPLOMATIC STUDIES AND STRATEGIES FOR GLOBAL SECURITY PROVIDES THE BASIC KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS IN THE FIELD OF CYBERSECURITY: FROM THE MATHEMATICAL TECHNIQUES FOR MODELING SYSTEMS TO THE ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLES AND SOFTWARE APPLICATION DESIGN TECHNIQUES, FROM THE CRYPTOGRAPHIC PRIMITIVES USED TO GUARANTEE THE SECURITY OF SYSTEMS TO THE SKILLS TO UNDERSTAND AND IMPLEMENT TECHNIQUES FOR PREVENTION AND MANAGEMENT OF SECURITY RISKS IN AN ORGANIZATIONAL AND ECONOMIC CONTEXT. THE CURRICULUM IN GEOPOLITICS FOR THE SECURITY OF THE MEDITERRANEAN PROVIDES THE ESSENTIAL KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS IN THE FIELD OF SECURITY APPLIED TO SOFT POWER, WITH PARTICULAR REGARD TO THE GEOPOLITICAL AREA OF THE "ENLARGED MEDITERRANEAN".

GRADUATES IN OTHER CLASSES MAY BE ADMITTED TO THE MASTER'S DEGREE COURSE IF THEY HAVE OBTAINED AT LEAST 40 ECTS WITHIN AT LEAST TWO OF THE FOLLOWING DISCIPLINARY AREAS: ECONOMIC, LEGAL, LINGUISTIC, SOCIOLOGICAL, HISTORICAL, POLITICAL. TO BE ADMITTED TO THE MASTER'S DEGREE COURSE, STUDENTS MUST ALSO HAVE ADEQUATE PERSONAL PREPARATION AND A GOOD KNOWLEDGE OF THE ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

IORIO Chairman of the didactic council GENNARO IORIO Characteristics and other information Specific learning objectives.
THE ADVANCED TRAINING COURSE ENTITLED SOCIO-RELATIONAL COUNSELING FOR HELPING PROFESSIONS AIMS TO FILL THE TRAINING GAP FOR THOSE PROFESSIONAL PROFILES THAT DEAL, IN ONE WAY OR ANOTHER, WITH HELPING RELATIONSHIPS AND THAT, COMING FROM MOSTLY THEORETICAL ACADEMIC BACKGROUNDS, NEED TO ACQUIRE TECHNICAL COMPETENCIES, ABILITIES AND PERSONAL ATTITUDES TO MANAGE THE WORK OF "TAKING CARE" EFFECTIVELY. THE COURSE AIMS AT THE FOLLOWING SPECIFIC LEARNING OBJECTIVES: TO INCREASE THE COMPETENCIES AND ABILITIES OF HELPING PROFESSIONALS TO ADDRESS PSYCHOSOCIAL NEEDS; TO BE ABLE TO VALUE EXPERIENCE AS A FUNDAMENTAL PREREQUISITE FOR LEARNING; TO STIMULATE THE RECOGNITION OF THE IMPACT OF CONTEXTUAL AND SITUATIONAL INFLUENCES ON SOCIAL IDENTITY; TO INCREASE THE INTEGRATION BETWEEN THEORY AND PRACTICE; TO PROMOTE AN "EMPOWERED-ORIENTED" APPROACH IN THE RELATIONSHIP WITH THE USER.

THE MASTER'S DEGREE COURSE PROVIDES PREPARATION THAT ENABLES STUDENTS TO PURSUE FURTHER STUDIES IN LEVEL II MASTER'S PROGRAMS AND RESEARCH DOCTORATE PROGRAMS IN THE AREA OF THEORETICAL AND APPLIED LINGUISTICS, FOREIGN LANGUAGES AND LITERATURES, AND LANGUAGE TEACHING. Professional status conferred by the degree:
- LITERARY AND SECTORAL LANGUAGE TRANSLATORS
- LANGUAGE AND CULTURAL CONSULTANTS
- LANGUAGE AND LITERARY TRAINERS
- LINGUISTIC-CULTURAL EXPERT FOR TERRITORIAL RESOURCES AND ECONOMIES
THE COURSE ALSO PREPARES STUDENTS FOR ADMISSION TO RESEARCH DOCTORATE PROGRAMS AND DOCTORAL SCHOOLS IN THE FIELD OF HUMANITIES. Characteristics of the final exam:
THE DEGREE IS AWARDED UPON SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF A FINAL EXAM. Social cooperatives, public and private territorial structures that deal with the reduction and prevention of discomfort at various levels and social and work reintegration. Examples:
social professional educator expert in reintegrating former prisoners, intercultural mediator, technician for assistance to young people with disabilities, technician for social mediation, expert in assistance for active elderly people (3.4.5.2.0). In fact, they can exploit their interdisciplinary training in order to use personally (or teach others) the linguistic structures they have acquired through the studies carried out in the Degree Course, applying these structures to institutional-business-cultural relations with foreign countries (they are, for example, able to write letters in a foreign language, prepare documents that use sector-specific languages, communicate by telephone in a foreign language, take notes in a foreign language, etc.) in the various multi-ethnic and multicultural contexts in which they may operate, both in Italy and abroad.

Characteristics of the final exam. To be admitted to the final exam, students must have regularly attended the training activities and obtained the credits provided for in the regulations. The final exam consists of the development of a technical-practical project, under the guidance of a supervisor. This project must synthesize as much as possible the basic and specific skills acquired during the three years of training. The result of this activity (which may or may not include a demonstrator) must be summarized in a report (written report) to accurately explain the activities carried out and the results obtained. The report must also reveal a correct use of sources and bibliography, systematic and argumentative skills, and clarity in the presentation. The project is discussed before a specially appointed commission. At the student's request, the final report can be prepared in English. Knowledge required for access. Professional Status conferred by the degree: Linguistic and intercultural mediator in social, tourist, cultural fields and in the field of international cooperation. In the cultural-touristic field, job opportunities fall within the various sectors related to cultural services and mediation between the cultures of different countries. The main job roles are: media operator; translator and expert in linguistic mediation in literary, artistic, and performing arts fields; tourist operator. Job opportunities in the socio-cultural field are mainly related, in Italy, to the needs of linguistic and cultural mediation connected to migration phenomena and to the design, in multilingual contexts, of cultural and tourist development, both tangible and intangible; abroad, to the activities of non-profit organizations and associations engaged in socio-economic and cultural development initiatives, as well as to embassies, consulates, and representative offices that maintain exchanges with European and non-European countries.

The final exam consists of a written paper of at least 30 pages and no more than 50 pages (or a multimedia paper of similar size). Historical-Artistic Area: At the end of the three-year period, graduates will have acquired a solid basic knowledge of the developments in the history of art from the ancient world to the contemporary era. The discipline is understood in its broadest methodological criteria: of studying artistic and architectural artifacts in their dual nature as material and cultural products, of the dynamics of creation and reception, of the physical and conservation events, and of the critical and collecting history. The course aims to stimulate critical analysis skills, develop skills in stylistic and iconographic reading of works of art, and understand the artifacts in relation to their contexts of belonging or origin, often altered or irreparably lost. The objective is to train figures capable of understanding, orienting, and operating in the field of historical-artistic heritage.

Candidates must produce, as a degree thesis, a written work with characteristics of originality that provides for a research effort adequate to the amount of training credits required. The work will focus on one of the scientific-disciplinary sectors of the planned training activities, within which the candidate has followed at least one course.

Persuasive and advertising communication: Graduates who follow the area in Persuasive and Advertising Communication will develop knowledge and understanding skills in relation to both the methods and the tools of persuasive communication, articulated in its two fundamental components: (i) public communication (which in turn can be divided into institutional, social and political communication); (ii) communication produced by companies (advertising and marketing strategies). The basis of these skills will be a broad and comprehensive reflection on: (i) communication models (from the pioneering communication research, to the models developed in the semiotic field, to those of interaction and inference proposed by pragmatics); (ii) theories and techniques of semiotic analysis of the text (advertising and media) (iii) techniques of rhetorical argumentation (including the theory of argumentative fallacies); (iv) sociological and psychological theories of communication; (v) theories and techniques of digital communication.

Historical Area: The Master's degree graduate in History must possess in-depth knowledge in the disciplinary areas characterizing the degree course, a solid ability to analyze sources and synthesize texts of historical literature. He/she must therefore be able to critically understand documents and original sources, thanks to the secure knowledge of the methods and languages characteristic of historical interpretation and reconstruction. This knowledge and skills must emerge both in the field of ancient and medieval history and in that of modern and contemporary history, also in relation to the use and enhancement of archival and documentary sources. Philosophical Area: The Master's degree graduate in Philosophy must possess in-depth knowledge in the disciplinary areas characterizing the degree course, a solid ability to analyze philosophical works and synthesize critical studies in philosophical and historical-philosophical fields.

Knowledge and understanding:
Area of communication learning: The basic knowledge is that specific to the founding disciplines of Communication Sciences (L-LIN/01, M-STO/04, SPS/04, SPS/08, L-FIL-LET/12, M-FIL/05); in particular, the socio-linguistic (L-FIL-LET/12) and semiotic (M-FIL/05) and anthropological (M-DEA/01) disciplines, with particular reference to disciplines of a philosophical-theoretical (M-FIL/01), psychological (M-PSI/01) and legal nature in the communicative field (IUS/01). The area of communication learning completes the basic critical knowledge with a series of advanced knowledge in the field of communication. The main forms and types of communication are examined during the educational path, each of which corresponds to one or more professional sectors. Around this framework of characterizing disciplines, students can draw on a selection of related and similar disciplines in different ways and from different perspectives in the disciplinary strands that are: Linguistic-cognitive disciplines, Historical-social disciplines, Languages of social communication and Techniques of communication.

Master's degree graduates acquire useful skills in a cross-cutting manner: they can carry out professional activities in companies and organizations, particularly in the area of administration, management control and corporate finance, as well as in all areas of Public Administrations, from the administrative departments of state bodies to state administrations, to local public bodies with particular reference to the tax agency, as well as in associations, institutions and private foundations with public purposes. Graduates may also carry out professional activities in the governing structures of national, European and international bodies, developing and implementing public intervention policies, also aimed at territorial management and in the field of tourism.

Historical-legal analysis of the contemporary international dimension: Master's degree graduates possess specialized knowledge relating to the political-institutional development and the functioning of international organizations in different areas of the globe, with particular reference to human rights, constitutionalism in areas of transition, the history of globalization and international relations.

Specific training objectives. The Master's Degree Course in Biology aims to train graduates with biomedical/pharmacological, physiological, biochemical and naturalistic skills, differently applied according to relevance in different application areas represented by two area curricula:
1. cellular-molecular;
2. nutritional. In addition, the training course is completed by Contextual knowledge and final exam. - CELLULAR-MOLECULAR AREA: Includes courses relevant to the acquisition of knowledge and skills in the cellular and biomolecular field, both in the basic and applied aspects, in areas such as the chemistry of biomolecules in -omics sciences (CHIM/06, BIO/10), cellular and molecular biology and biodiversity in human, animal and plant contexts (BIO/01-03, BIO/05-07, BIO/11, BIO/18) and biomedical microbiology (BIO/19, MED/07, MED/42).

Genetic counseling assistants: The Master's degree graduate in Genetic Counselling has professional opportunities in both private and public organizations that offer genetic counseling services. Characteristics of the final exam: The final exam for obtaining the Master's Degree in Genetic Counselling, which is worth 12 credits, consists of writing a thesis developed in an original way by the student under the supervision of a supervisor. The thesis is the result of the studies and research conducted during the last year of the course. The final exam is discussed orally before an appropriate examining board, which evaluates the merit score based on the following criteria: originality of the topic of the paper, expository skills both in writing and orally, research methodologies. The grade for the final degree exam is expressed in hundredths, with possible honors. Knowledge and understanding:
Human Genetics: The Master's degree graduate in Genetic Counselling must have knowledge of human genetics, medical genetics, and laboratory genetics. Therefore, it is necessary for them to acquire basic knowledge: i) of human genetics, ii) of molecular biology, iii) of the molecular mechanisms responsible for pathology, iv) of the available techniques for their identification, including the latest generation technologies; v) of typical and atypical inheritance patterns, vi) of how to calculate the probabilities of disease occurrence in individuals and offspring. Knowledge and understanding are acquired through lectures and curricular internship activities and are verified through ongoing tests and final exams in each specific sector.

LABOR CONSULTANT: To practice the profession of labor consultant, the graduate must complete a mandatory internship period at the office of an accredited labor consultant for a duration of eighteen months, six of which may also be completed during the third year of the degree course, in accordance with the agreement signed between the University of Siena and the Provincial Council of Labor Consultants of Siena. Once the certification of completed training has been obtained, the interested party may participate in the annual accreditation exam, organized on a regional basis following the relevant announcement issued by decree of the Ministry of Labor. Once the accreditation exam has been passed, the new labor consultant may register with the Council of the Order in the province where he/she intends to practice the profession. The labor consultant can operate in a freelance capacity, with his/her own office, or in companies, public or private, trade unions, associations representing typical professional interests in the world of work and business.

Specialist Social Worker
Master's graduates in Social Sustainability and Welfare Management can take the state exam to qualify for the profession and register in the A register of specialist social workers. The specialist social worker can work, also with management and leadership functions, in public bodies (ASL, Prefectures, Ministries - Justice, Labor, Health, etc. - Local authorities, etc.). Furthermore, the Master's graduate in Social Sustainability and Welfare Management can work in management positions in Third Sector organizations (social cooperatives, volunteer associations, NGOs, foundations, mutual aid societies, etc.) and private companies (residential facilities for the elderly, minors, asylum seekers, etc.). This professional can also carry out independent professional activities in the areas of consulting, research and social design. Characteristics of the final exam: The final exam consists of the discussion of a thesis chosen by the student in a course among those present in the individual study plan and on a topic agreed with the teacher responsible for that course (thesis supervisor). Program, texts and objectives: Professional status conferred by the degree. Audio-Prosthetist Technician.
The Audio-Prosthetist Technician works under supervision or as a freelance consultant in public or private organizations that deal with audiological rehabilitation in both childhood and adulthood. Characteristics of the final exam: Pursuant to Article 6, paragraph 3, of Legislative Decree No. 502/1992 and subsequent amendments, and Article 6 of the Interministerial Decree of February 19, 2009 (Determination of the degree classes of health professions), the final exam of the Degree Course has the value of a state exam enabling the exercise of the profession. The final exam consists of a practical test, in which the student must demonstrate that they have acquired the theoretical and practical knowledge and technical-operational skills, and the preparation of a thesis, assigned under the guidance of a supervisor and discussed with the commission and the co-supervisor. The final exam is worth 5 CFU. Knowledge required for admission: To be admitted to the Degree Course in Audio-Prosthetic Techniques, applicants must have a secondary school diploma or another qualification obtained abroad, recognized as suitable.

The Audio-Prosthetist Technician works under supervision or as a freelance consultant in public or private organizations that deal with audiological rehabilitation in both childhood and adulthood. Language(s) of instruction and assessment. ITALIAN. Competencies associated with the function. Audio-Prosthetist Technician. The activity of the Audio-Prosthetist Technician is aimed at the application of prosthetic aids by taking the impression of the external auditory canal, the construction and application of ear molds or other acoustic coupling systems and the administration of prosthetic evaluation tests. The Audio-Prosthetist Technician has didactic and scientific skills in Audiological Prosthetics and can be included in multidisciplinary teams for clinical and research activities. Function in the work context. Audio-Prosthetist Technician. The Audio-Prosthetist Technician is responsible for the selection, supply, fitting and control of prosthetic aids for the prevention and correction of hearing loss; provides counseling for the use of hearing aids and operates on the doctor's prescription through professional acts that imply full responsibility and the consequent autonomy.

Characteristics of the final exam: The final exam consists of preparing and publicly discussing a thesis, which can be either a compilation or an experimental thesis, developed originally by the student, under the supervision of a teacher from a relevant academic field within the course of study, and related to a topic relevant to the curricular disciplines. The compilation thesis consists of an in-depth bibliographic study on a topic agreed upon between the teacher and the student, and the writing of an original written work. The experimental thesis consists of conducting original research or collecting and processing original information from clinical-scientific databases. The experimental thesis can be carried out in a university laboratory, a company, or a research institution, in Italy or abroad, with which the University has established a convention or international agreement. The final exam includes the completion of a practical test to evaluate the professional skills acquired during the practical internship, which precedes the discussion of the degree thesis and aims to assess the candidate's level of technical preparation for the authorization to practice the profession.

Master's degree graduates acquire knowledge and the ability to understand and elaborate concepts in the chemical, biological, pharmaceutical and pharmacological fields. In particular, they acquire knowledge of the scientific approach to solving problems related to the structural design of biologically active molecules, synthesis, development, evaluation of biological and/or pharmacological activity, preparation of the pharmaceutical form, quality control in production, patent and drug registration procedures, as well as knowledge of the legislative contexts in which pharmaceutical industries and pharmacies operate. By consulting scientific literature, the master's degree graduate must be able to quickly assimilate the scientific and technological innovations that are occurring rapidly in these areas and be able to develop and apply original ideas that are up to the state of the art, even in a research context. The verification of learning involves traditional exams in which the candidate demonstrates to a commission of experts in the subject their ability to assimilate and integrate the knowledge acquired and to communicate it clearly and unambiguously.

Thematic area 1: Starting from the basic knowledge of organic chemistry, the student must know the problems of the molecular structures associated with the various classes of drugs, deepening the aspects related to the structure/activity relationships and the processes of synthesis and production of active ingredients. The student must understand the main models of study of the pharmaceutical activity of an organic molecule, its pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, always at the molecular level. The student must understand the main modes of operation of an active ingredient, correlating the molecular structures with the biological properties of the molecules, including their toxicology. Through the practical exercises, which consist of 4 single-station laboratories for a total of 160 hours of activity, the student will have the opportunity to put into practice the theoretical knowledge acquired in the various courses, being able to carry out analyses and preparations of pharmaceutical active ingredients. The student must also learn the use of the main laboratory instruments, demonstrating that they are able to process the experimental data obtained.

The Master's Thesis can be of a descriptive or theoretical-experimental nature. In any case, the final exam aims to highlight the skills acquired by the student for the study, understanding, critical evaluation and design of advanced and original solutions in the scientific/technological field. The final paper consists of a short paper, accompanied by the necessary bibliographic references, on a theoretical or empirical topic chosen by the student according to the procedures defined in a regulation on the final exam prepared by the competent teaching structure. - high skills in carrying out and managing bibliographic, archival and iconographic research

- high ability to express oneself in writing and orally, both at a scientific and popular level
- ability to work in a team and to interact with different professionals
- ability to design and direct an exhibition event of a historical-artistic nature
- good knowledge of the English language, and possibly other languages of the European Union. Description of admission tests. Test to verify the student's personal preparation

ose one of the three areas in which the discipline is articulated, namely Medieval Art, Modern Art and Contemporary Art.
Secondly, the course also includes more operational aspects than the historical-critical ones, which are, however, closely related, relating to the field of contemporary museums and the protection and conservation of artistic heritage, according to an approach capable of bringing students into contact with specific working contexts. In the first year, the training objectives focus on a solid preparation with respect to the artistic and architectural manifestations from the early Middle Ages to the present day and their critical analysis (historical-artistic learning area, 24 credits), which, based on the knowledge acquired in the Bachelor's degree, can be further deepened in terms of the topics covered. Also in the first year, and following the area chosen by the student (Medieval Art, Modern Art or Contemporary Art), these deepening will be accompanied by an indispensable knowledge of the contemporary historical events, without which a full understanding of the motivations, genesis and outcomes of artistic and architectural production would be impossible (historical learning area, 12 credits).

Also in the first year, a course focused on contemporary museography is included, which represents a first approach to one of the possible employment opportunities for Master's graduates in Art History, namely museums. The knowledge of the historical and contemporary methods of "presenting" cultural heritage in its museographic and museological components aims to develop in the student a critical awareness of the fundamental operation of exhibition choices and to provide him/her with the basic tools to deal with the complex work in the museum field.

For graduates in the LM-1 Master's degree class, the field of volunteering and public intervention in the social sphere is also open, as far as concerns bodies that are interested in phenomena such as migration flows and policies of reception and control of processes of exclusion (racism, gender discrimination) and dependence (forms of access to work, to political representation).

Characteristics of the final exam The final exam consists of a public discussion, before a commission composed of a number of teachers indicated in the University and Department Regulations, of a thesis, which is the product of original research and the result of an organic personal re-elaboration of knowledge acquired during the training course. They must also demonstrate the candidate's ability to present clearly and effectively and to adequately argue the results of his/her research work. The thesis work will be carried out under the supervision of one of the teachers of the Course and will be discussed with the participation of a co-supervisor. The evaluation of the final exam will be expressed in hundredths with possible honors.

General Area The training course for students in the Master's Degree Course aims at building and developing a solid professional preparation, through the provision of lessons dedicated to deepening the procedures and purposes of research, protection, conservation and enhancement of archaeological heritage. The training space allowed by the two-year period will allow the student to identify a Study Plan whose contents are proposed within aggregations of disciplines created with logical sense, identifiable in chronological order in the three macro-themes of Prehistoric Archaeology, Classical Archaeology and Medieval Archaeology. The student will also be guided in the construction of his/her Study Plan to achieve a greater level of in-depth study in the area of his/her interest, subject to approval by the Teaching Committee of the Master's Degree Course in Archaeology.

Based on these design lines, the Course offers a course structured in two years:
Year 1 The student will be able to acquire a solid cultural base on the archaeologies of the Mediterranean and European area in relation to the themes of Prehistoric and Protohistoric Archaeology, Classical Archaeology and Medieval Archaeology. Some in-depth studies will concern: historical, philological and demo-ethno-anthropological disciplines; the museumization and management of archaeological heritage; the most advanced methodologies applied to landscape archaeology, excavation techniques, the reading and interpretation of archaeological contexts and the most modern archaeometric technologies. Year 2 Specific in-depth studies are planned, providing the student with further historical, archaeological, computer and legislative skills in the archaeological sector. In the second year, the student has the opportunity to deepen the experience in the field, through participation in excavations, experimental research projects, internships and training internships, together with the acquisition of linguistic skills and the preparation of a final exam, preparatory to the award of the Master's Degree.

Master's degree graduates in Modern Literature may carry out professional activities in local authorities and specific institutions, such as libraries, archives and academies, as well as in publishing houses, editorial offices, foundations, companies and other professional bodies operating in the organization of events and cultural activities. Characteristics of the final exam. The final exam consists of the discussion of an original thesis consistent with the training objectives of the study course, developed under the guidance of a supervisor and discussed before a commission.

Textbooks will be chosen based on their scientific level, their updating with respect to the state of research, the transparency of their content, and their methodological effectiveness. Knowledge and understanding
Generic Area
The Master's degree graduate in Classical Studies will possess:
* Solid and advanced disciplinary knowledge, both content-based and methodological, relating to the ancient and medieval world, understood in its chronological, spatial and thematic complexity. * Ability to critically use literary and extra-literary sources, as well as other knowledge tools (specialist texts, databases, various types of computer supports) to build their own organic and solid system of knowledge about the ancient world, with particular reference to the specific disciplinary area chosen. * Knowledge of ancient languages at a level that allows them to be used to build autonomous critical elaborations with reference to the specific field of study chosen. * Specific theoretical, methodological and operational knowledge relating to the chosen disciplinary area and the peculiar forms in which modern philological and linguistic research, as well as historical and archaeological research, are expressed in it.

Characteristics of the final exam: The final exam consists of (D.I. 19 February 2009, art. 7):
a) a practical test during which the student must demonstrate that they have acquired the theoretical and practical knowledge and skills, as well as the technical and operational skills specific to the professional profile. b) drafting of a thesis and its discussion. The final exam is evaluated by a Commission. It consists of at least seven and no more than eleven members and includes at least two members appointed by the Professional Order, identified according to current regulations. During this test, the student must demonstrate that they have acquired scientific and theoretical-practical preparation, a methodology and skills that allow them professional, decision-making and operational autonomy for the exercise of the profession.

Graduates in physiotherapy must have acquired the following knowledge and understanding:
a) knowledge of the biochemical and genetic mechanisms underlying human life, including the biological phenomena that occur in the cell and tissues;
b) ability to understand the structure of the human body and know its physiological mechanisms of functioning, with particular reference to the somatic and autonomic nervous system, the musculoskeletal and cardiovascular-respiratory system;
c) knowledge of the elements of psychology underlying the relationships between people, especially in a healthcare setting, and the pedagogical principles for correct communication and interpersonal relationships;
d) knowledge of the mechanisms of the organism's response to the main pathogenic factors and the etiology and pathogenesis of the main acute and chronic pathologies of interest to physiotherapy, including the general effects of their treatment. Area of Physiotherapy Sciences.

b) knowledge of the etiopathogenesis and clinical manifestations of disorders of the musculoskeletal, neurological, cardiovascular-respiratory, visceral system, in all age groups;

The graduate in Medical Radiology Techniques for Imaging and Radiotherapy is a health professional who provides his/her services in the departments and services of Diagnostic Imaging, Radiotherapy or Nuclear Medicine of hospital and non-hospital facilities of the NHS and in similar private facilities and in scientific research and care institutes. He/she can also be employed in industries producing, sales agencies operating in the specific sector of diagnostic and therapeutic equipment and supplies, in general. The Technician also finds employment in university and extra-university research centers in the biomedical sector, and can also carry out independent professional activities. Characteristics of the final exam: The final exam has the value of a state exam enabling the exercise of the profession (Legislative Decree 502/1992, art. 6, paragraph 3) and consists of:
a) a practical test during which the student must demonstrate that he/she has acquired the theoretical and practical knowledge and skills and the technical-operational skills specific to the professional profile;
b) preparation of a thesis and its discussion. See DM 19 February 2009, art. 7.

Knowledge and Understanding: Cardiopulmonary Physiopathology: The graduate must have demonstrated a broad spectrum of knowledge and critical understanding of the physiopathological response of adult and pediatric patients with congenital and acquired heart diseases. Basic Techniques of Extracorporeal Circulation: The graduate must demonstrate extensive knowledge of current clinical technologies, which must include at least:
a. Cardiopulmonary bypass. b. Pumps, hemofiltration, gas exchange, oxygenators, hemodilution, myocardial protection and preservation, thermal regulation, perfusion circuits, pharmacological interventions, techniques for blood preservation including autotransfusion, platelet gel production, acute normovolemic hemodilution and bloodletting, monitoring, analysis and management of anticoagulation and hemostasis. Characteristics of the final exam: The final exam consists of a discussion of a written paper prepared independently by the student, under the guidance of a lecturer, during the internship/stage period, which can be carried out at the university or an external company. The purpose of the final exam is to ascertain that the graduate has acquired knowledge and understanding skills in the field of biology, that they are able to elaborate them individually and apply this knowledge in a working context. The final exam consists of the presentation of the paper in a concise form and a discussion of its contents before a Degree Commission. At the end of the presentation and discussion of the paper, the supervisor proposes an assessment, up to a maximum of four points, in relation to the commitment and preparation demonstrated by the student during the internship/stage, while the Degree Commission proposes an assessment up to a maximum of four points, in relation to the written, oral presentation and discussion skills demonstrated by the student.

The Master's Degree Course is characterized by the presence of two areas of knowledge: that of Ecotoxicology and that of Environmental Sustainability. The two areas prove to be perfectly complementary since they address the problems related to the influence of human activity on ecosystems from two different points of view: the more analytical one of Ecotoxicology and the more systemic one of Environmental Sustainability. In the Master's degree program, the student must be able to manage the information and knowledge offered by both scientific proposals in order to have, once graduated, a complete picture of the complexity of human-nature relationships and the skills to professionally manage the problems that these relationships progressively generate.

Category: Economics, Management and Law. Regulatory Framework: 270/04. Degree Class: L-18 - Class of Degrees in Economics and Business Management. Verification of required knowledge for access: No. Program, texts and objectives: Specific learning objectives of the course and description of the educational path. The Bachelor's Degree in Business Management aims to train professionals capable of understanding, managing and improving the processes through which companies create value, efficiently transforming production factors into goods and services that meet the needs of consumers or users.

To develop these skills, Business Management graduates learn the tools for detection and analysis and the decision-making models typical of management disciplines, and are guided in their application, also using appropriate mathematical and statistical methodologies and IT tools. They also know how to grasp the connections between the company and the economic and regulatory context, thanks to the acquisition of the fundamental interpretative tools of economics and law. In the first year, common to all degree courses in the same class, students explore the typical themes of Economics, Business Economics and Law, as well as acquiring the necessary basic mathematical-analytical and statistical skills. Subsequently, the Business Management degree course provides specific in-depth studies in the various fields of management knowledge, legal integrations for commercial aspects and the study of foreign languages, with some limited degrees of freedom for students in their choices.

Knowledge required for access: The student enrolling in the Business Management degree course is required to demonstrate possession of a minimum level of knowledge in the following areas:
- mastery of the basic tools of logic and mathematics with particular reference to:
° elementary algebraic calculation: powers, absolute value,
polynomials, first and second degree equations and inequalities;
° fundamental notions of analytical geometry: straight line,
circle, parabola, ellipse and hyperbola;
- mastery of a foreign language at level B1, among French, English, German and Spanish;
- mastery of personal productivity applications (Open Office, Microsoft Office, etc.), ECDL level, or equivalent (4 basic modules, designed to be integrated with learning during the course of study, up to ECDL Full level, or equivalent). Category: Economics, Management and Law. Regulatory Framework: Reform 270/04. Degree Class: L-33 - Class of degrees in Economics. Location: City Campus - Economics - via Inama, 5 (Sustainable capacity: 235). Department: Department of Economics and Management. Verification of knowledge required for access: No. Program, texts and objectives: Specific learning objectives of the course and description of the educational path. The Bachelor's Degree in Economics and Management aims to provide a solid methodological foundation in economics and management sciences, enabling students to correctly and effectively master economic analysis at both the country and company levels, with particular attention to the growing interrelationships between the two areas.

Graduates in Economics and Management will be able to directly and independently address tasks and decision-making problems in various fields, using up-to-date analytical, measurement, and forecasting tools. The Bachelor's Degree in Economics and Management also aims to provide training that is open to continuous learning and innovation, allowing graduates to subsequently access the latest developments in the field during their professional career or further education. The Economics and Management course is a course with an exclusively "methodological" focus and is therefore strongly oriented towards providing solid and in-depth basic knowledge in the reference disciplines and analytical tools. To this end, particular emphasis is placed on the acquisition of mathematical and statistical tools, with particular attention to the inferential aspects of statistics. The course of study includes an initial part dedicated to the fundamentals of economic and management disciplines, with theoretical and methodological in-depth study.

In particular, the basic knowledge of economics and management will be explored, with interrelationships between the two areas, especially with regard to markets, consumer behavior, and competition. In this area of basic training, the typical themes of regulation and the formation of the norms that underpin them will be addressed. In addition, there will also be courses with a general educational value, such as economic history. In the second part of the course, students will explore some areas of theory typical of the common areas of interest of economics and management, paying attention to the theme of economic decision-making. This theme will be explored both at the analytical level and at the level of behavioral aspects, the study of which is now a fundamental part of the knowledge base for those involved in economic decisions, both at the aggregate level and at the company level. This is in line with the prevailing orientations of the Faculty, which are oriented towards behavioral studies. Finally, students will have the opportunity to orient their training by choosing from a range of thematic in-depth courses in the various areas of study previously addressed.

Knowledge required for access: Students enrolling in the Bachelor's Degree in Economics and Management are required to demonstrate possession of a minimum level of knowledge in the following areas:
- mastery of the basic tools of logic and mathematics, with particular reference to:
• elementary algebraic calculation: powers, absolute value, polynomials, first and second degree equations and inequalities;
• fundamental notions of analytical geometry: line, circle, parabola, ellipse and hyperbola;
- mastery of a foreign language at level B1, among French, English, German and Spanish;
- mastery of personal productivity applications (Open Office, Microsoft Office, etc.), ECDL level or equivalent (4 basic modules, to be integrated with learning during the course of study, up to ECDL Full or equivalent). Verification of the knowledge required for access is provided, according to the methods defined by the didactic regulations of the course of study, which also identifies any additional training obligations in the event of a negative verification.

ational and multinational, non-profit organizations, and public bodies and administrations operating in various sectors.
The aim of the Master's Degree is to train professionals capable of managing the main company functions, in the various contexts, both through full mastery of analysis techniques and knowledge for supporting decision-making processes, and by coordinating and organizing operational units. The curriculum of the Master's Degree in Management is also designed with the aim of activating a "parallel" degree course (ex DM 50/2010, §31) entirely in English with the same learning objectives and career opportunities. The parallel course, organized and managed in partnership with foreign universities, provides for students to spend significant periods (at least one year) at other universities and obtain a joint degree recognized in various countries, or a double degree. The internship usually involves a period at a company to address a specific problem of direct interest to the company, under the guidance of a company tutor and an academic tutor. The degree thesis is an important moment of in-depth study, including theoretical and conceptual aspects, of typical management topics, and is accompanied by an empirical part.

- curricular requirements:
o possession of a first-level degree, obtained at Italian Universities or another qualification obtained abroad, recognized as suitable;
o at least a B1 level or equivalent proficiency in English;
- specific preparation requirements:
o demonstrate good skills in reading and commenting on data relating to the economic performance of companies and the economic-financial context;
o demonstrate good analytical skills in addressing quantitative problems;
o have adequate familiarity with the basic techniques of descriptive statistics;
o have good analytical skills for economic and business problems. The knowledge usually includes the equivalent of at least 60 ECTS relating to courses belonging to the basic and characterizing scientific-disciplinary sectors of degree classes 17 and 28 (ex DM. 509/99) or degree classes 18 and 33 (ex DM. 270/04). The Degree Course trains engineers with in-depth methodological and operational knowledge in the basic scientific disciplines (mathematics, physics, chemistry, computer science) and broad skills in the engineering disciplines, with particular emphasis on those specific to industrial engineering for a modern and advanced approach to the complexity of typical industrial manufacturing problems.

ndustrial engineering for a modern and advanced approach to the complexity of typical industrial manufacturing problems.
The specific objective of the degree course is the training of system engineers oriented towards the manufacturing industry, who have acquired tools for understanding subsystems of different nature (in particular, mechanical, technological, electrical, electronic and computer science) and strong skills in functional integration; they must also know conventional and innovative materials, the development of related production technologies, the management of industrial processes and plants, and the organization of companies, without neglecting the fundamental skills of information engineering, necessary both to ensure a rational use of the potential offered by information technologies and to understand their impact on production realities. The Degree Course intends to provide, from different points of view, an overall vision oriented to the life cycle of industrial products and related production processes, in a form useful for developing any material good, including the same tools and production processes, with particular attention to the processes of development of new technologies and new products, their cognitive and connectivity functionalities.

The natural outcome of the educational path is access to a second-level degree course, although the preparation is also adequate for entering the world of work. The educational path is structured over three years, providing a first year mainly dedicated to the teaching of basic disciplines, a second year to complete the basic training to which the main characterizing teachings of industrial engineering are added, which draw on the scientific knowledge acquired with the study of the basic disciplines and provide the methodological and operational knowledge necessary for the completion of the training, which takes place during the third year in which the student can access a wide range of specific teachings of industrial engineering. The third year is completed by elective courses, evenly distributed over the two semesters, and the final exam. Activities dedicated to the development of knowledge useful for entering the world of work and those for knowledge of the English language are evenly distributed over the three years. It is possible to offer students non-compulsory courses in English. The educational objectives of the degree course will be achieved through the articulation of the educational offer in educational paths that will share all the basic teachings and a solid core of characterizing teachings of industrial engineering.

The Degree Course in Industrial Engineering requires adequate skills and knowledge from the candidates, in particular:
- ability to understand verbal communication and to communicate effectively in writing and orally in Italian;
- adequate knowledge of the English language (as established in the Regulations of the Degree Course);
- ability to logical deductive reasoning;
- ability to analyze the behavior of a simple system starting from the fundamental laws and the characteristics of its components;
- ability to distinguish between necessary and sufficient condition;
- ability to distinguish between definition, theorem and demonstration. Basic knowledge in Mathematics (Arithmetic and algebra, Analytical geometry and numerical functions, Trigonometry, Statistics, computer science), in Physical and chemical sciences (Mechanics, Optics, Thermodynamics, Electromagnetism, Chemistry and structure of matter) is also required. To access the degree course, candidates must take the entrance test for Engineering organized on a national basis by the Interuniversity Center for Access to Schools of Engineering and Architecture (CISIA) and an English language proficiency test.

The Master's Degree in Civil Engineering is aimed at training highly qualified professionals who are prepared to address and solve in a coordinated manner the complex design, operational, organizational and management issues that characterize the civil engineering sector or that require an interdisciplinary approach; it consolidates the knowledge acquired in the previous degree program in basic scientific disciplines such as physics, mathematics and in the disciplines of civil engineering, achieving high levels of ability to design, plan, program and manage complex systems, processes and services, in particular in the area of small and large structures, in the area of structural rehabilitation and conservation, in the design of infrastructure works and integrated design with solid knowledge and skills in new digital technologies.

The second year is entirely dedicated to specific training, which differs depending on the different areas of choice, but all of which aim to offer students not only theoretical, technical and regulatory knowledge and skills, but also design skills in areas that allow for in-depth study and specialization:
- in the design, analysis, construction and control of structures in civil and industrial fields, with reference to traditional materials (concrete, steel, wood) and advanced materials (composite materials, metamaterials) and with particular attention to exceptional actions (fire, earthquake, NaTech events, etc.);
- in the rehabilitation of civil and industrial structures, with attention to the reduction of seismic vulnerability and the compatibility of interventions with the principles of conservation (reversibility, minimal impact) and environmental sustainability (use of sustainable materials such as wood), also with reference to buildings of historical or monumental interest;
- in the design, construction, management and maintenance of infrastructure works (roads, bridges and hydraulic works), underground structures, retaining structures and foundations, with strong skills in new digital technologies (sensors, telecommunications, data inversion techniques, optimization and artificial intelligence, decision support systems);
- in the integrated design of buildings developed in a digital BIM/HBIM (Building Information Modeling/Heritage Building Information Modeling) environment in the various phases of ideation, construction, management, maintenance and decommissioning, with particular regard to energy saving, living comfort and innovation of technical/technological systems in new and existing civil works.

The themes of ethics and professional deontology are specifically addressed by professionals in the field, as part of a specific agreement that the Department of Civil, Environmental and Mechanical Engineering has with the professional orders of engineers through seminars proposed within specific teaching activities.  - Program, texts and objectives: Specific educational objectives of the course and description of the educational path.
The Master's graduate in Environmental and Territorial Engineering is able to design, plan, design and manage works, systems, plants and services in various areas of interest of civil-environmental engineering, which are explored within specific curricula in different thematic areas, such as:
- the protection of the territory from natural and anthropogenic hazards, the analysis of danger and the mitigation of hydrogeological risk, the protection and rehabilitation of environmental water bodies;
- urban and river hydraulic infrastructures and works, reinforcement and protection works of defense systems, and in general civil works within the territorial context;
- sustainable management of environmental resources, the treatment of emissions in solid, liquid and gaseous form, the monitoring of quality, the prevention of pollution and the remediation of environmental matrices (air, water, soil);
- the management of the territory and the built environment, even in the presence of conflicting uses of resources, with a view to environmental sustainability and within specific socio-economic contexts.

Furthermore, the Master's graduate in Environmental and Territorial Engineering is able to:
- select and therefore use mathematical and numerical models in a conscious way;
- use techniques and technologies for the acquisition and analysis of data for environmental monitoring;
- analyze and interpret environmental data characterized by considerable complexity;
- analyze and evaluate the environmental impact of civil and industrial works and develop procedures for strategic environmental assessment of territorial plans and programs;
- interact with experts from different disciplines in order to solve complex environmental problems. The educational path includes a core of common lessons, mainly in the first year and taught in English, with the aim of providing the typical skills of the engineer who works in the civil-environmental field, combining them with the ability to use numerical tools for the modeling of environmental processes and the knowledge of the approaches of ecologically oriented territorial planning. The methods and skills acquired in the common lessons are functional to deepen the more applicative aspects that are addressed in curricula focused on specific themes.

Knowledge required for access: To enroll in the Master's Degree Course in Environmental and Territorial Engineering, it is necessary to have a degree or another qualification obtained abroad recognized as suitable. Access is direct in the case of a degree or university diploma obtained at the end of a course of study lasting at least three years in the degree class L-7 (DM 270/04) or in class 8 (DM 509/99), or a qualification obtained abroad recognized as suitable. In the case of a degree or university diploma, obtained at the end of a course of study lasting at least three years, in classes other than those indicated in the previous point or other qualification obtained abroad, access to the course of study is also subject to the possession of the following minimum curricular requirements:
- 24 CFU in the SSDs MAT/03, MAT/05, MAT/06, MAT/07, MAT/08;
- 18 CFU in the SSDs CHIM/06, CHIM/07, FIS/01, FIS/03, ING-IND/10, ING-IND/11, ING-IND/22;
- 30 CFU in the SSDs ICAR/01, ICAR/02, ICAR/03, ICAR/06, ICAR/07;

Admission requires knowledge of the English language at a level not lower than B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference. For students who are not native Italian speakers - or who have not completed a higher education cycle in that language - who intend to choose a curriculum with compulsory lessons in Italian, knowledge of the Italian language at least at level B2 is also required.
