COURSE STRUCTURE The course of study provides a basic training, common to all engineering degrees, followed by a broad engineering training in the area of information engineering. Subsequently, the course of study is structured in paths in which the student, at his/her own choice, will acquire specific and in-depth training in one of the areas that characterize information engineering, such as computer engineering, telecommunications engineering, or electronic engineering. In order to allow the student to acquire and integrate the various knowledge required in a harmonious and balanced way, the educational offer is structured in:
1) a basic training in which both the methodological-operational aspects of mathematics and the fundamental knowledge and methodological aspects of the basic sciences of interest for information technologies are dealt with;
2) a broad engineering training in the area of information engineering, in which the fundamental contents of the disciplines that characterize the information area (electronics, computer science and telecommunications) and the knowledge of the related methodologies are acquired.

The educational path aims to respond to the strong demand for skills expressed by the world of work and, in particular, by the industrial sector, where engineers are increasingly called upon to:
- manage complex systems with a holistic vision, ensuring attention to the various factors that contribute to determining overall performance in the industrial field;
- design, manage and improve industrial processes, both of a production and logistics nature, and of an organizational nature;
- manage technological and organizational innovation by adopting multi- and interdisciplinary approaches;
- promote the development of new production and economic paradigms deriving from the cognitive and connectivity potential offered by recent developments in digital technologies, while managing the profound changes in roles and operational contexts that result from them;
- combine technical knowledge and skills with economic and organizational knowledge and skills.

Basic sciences are primarily interpreted as disciplines aimed at the functional description of the mechatronic system, understood as a set of subsystems that interact at multiple levels (mechanical, electronic, computer) and that increasingly integrate cognitive and interconnection capabilities. The training aims to develop transversal skills that allow the student to organize the necessary connections between disciplines, understanding the experimental purpose (through physical laboratories and/or simulations) of the learning process. The organization of the educational path is based on a first year aimed at providing students with the fundamental theoretical tools of numerical analysis and mechatronics (mechanics, automation, signals and measurements), consolidating the ability to understand, formalize, model, simulate and control an intelligent mechanical system. The second year completes the training by focusing on specific in-depth studies of advanced mechanics, dynamics, distributed systems, robotics, innovative control applications and intelligent transport systems, organized according to the curricula of the degree program.

The general educational objective of the degree program is to train graduates with solid cultural foundations in the engineering field and with specific knowledge related to the production processes, properties, development and applications of materials, the design, development and innovation of products, the management of the product life cycle in line with the current evolution of modern manufacturing industry, where a systems approach prevails, which is necessary for the application of sustainability criteria and for the implementation of the principles of the circular economy.

The achievement of the educational objectives provided for by the degree program takes place through an educational path in which, in the first common year, the fundamental theoretical-practical tools relating to the chemistry and physics of condensed matter, thermodynamics, the structure and properties of the various classes of materials, the related production processes are provided within compulsory and characterizing educational activities, consolidating the ability to understand their functioning, design their application, evaluate their degradation in use, and plan their restoration. The second year provides for specific educational activities relating to advanced materials, modern production technologies, methods for product design and development, strategies for managing materials throughout their life cycle, with particular attention to sustainability and recycling.

Taking advantage of the possibility of providing additional courses compared to those provided for by the Degree Class (MUR Decree of December 19, 2023), the program extends the characterizing activities with respect to the reference SSDs ING-INF/06 and ING-IND/34, adding two preparatory disciplines to consolidate the engineering skills useful for the development of technologies and tools for advanced biomedical applications with reference to the area of materials and electronics for bio and electro-medical applications. To this end, the courses of Biomedical Engineering: ING-IND/34 and ING-INF/06 are identified as characterizing elements of the Master's Degree program, for a total of 39 ECTS. These are supplemented by the engineering disciplines of science and technology of materials (ING-IND/22) and electronics (ING-INF/01), for a total of 12 ECTS, as basic elements for consolidating knowledge in the areas of industrial engineering and computer and electronics engineering, which constitute the training pillars of the new program.

The courses of biomedical disciplines relating to the themes of physiology and biology and medical disciplines also represent an essential complementary training, for the development of skills aimed at the development of technologies and tools for personalized and precision medicine. Finally, the multi- and interdisciplinary training will be guaranteed by a set of related and integrative activities aimed at consolidating engineering skills in the areas of biomechanics, computer science, medical robotics and fluid dynamics. The set of these courses will provide the graduate with the fundamental skills for the development and evaluation of medical instrumentation, devices and implants, on biomaterials and related advanced manufacturing methods, the processing of biomedical data and signals, the physiology of systems, the principles of diagnostics for personalized medicine and the representation of medical-biological knowledge through advanced modeling. These skills constitute the knowledge base for the development of enabling technologies for modern patient-centered medicine.

rical and critical training in linguistic, philological and literary disciplines from antiquity to the contemporary era.
In particular, the course aims to provide the following skills:
- Ability to analyze any type of text in all its linguistic, philological, stylistic, historical-literary aspects;
- Ability to elaborate complex texts;
- Ability to organize and produce texts of a compilative nature;
- Textual and editing skills;
- Ability to use the main IT tools in specific areas of competence. Graduates must therefore possess solid knowledge of literature and linguistics, with particular experience in the direct analysis of texts and documents. They must demonstrate full mastery of a language of the EU, in addition to Italian. The methods of delivery of the courses included in the educational path correspond to the types of lectures and seminars; lectures and seminars aim to develop students' critical and expository skills, both oral and written. The educational path provides for the specialist study of themes relating to the cultural heritage transmitted from classical civilization to Italian literature, through the Romance world, within the framework of European literary civilization.

- Classical Philology: focused on the study of Greek and Latin language and literature;
- Modern Philology: focused on the linguistic and philological study of medieval and modern literatures with particular reference to Italian literature. Knowledge required for access

24 CFU in the following sectors: L-FIL-LET/10 Italian Literature, L-FIL-LET/11 Contemporary Italian Literature, L-FIL-LET/12 Italian Linguistics, L-FIL-LET/13 Philology of Italian Literature, L-FIL-LET/14 Literary Criticism and Comparative Literature. Students who do not have the credits required for access may obtain them by enrolling in individual courses at the undergraduate level. The Computer Science graduate is a professional with the ability to analyze complex systems (companies, services, natural and artificial systems), identify crucial processes in a systematic way, and propose models and solutions that can be implemented through software and computer systems. The mindset, given the emphasis on universal scientific tools and methods, is naturally predisposed to quickly integrate into different work contexts, adapting to the rapid innovation that characterizes the sector. The degree course provides a common set of courses in which basic skills in mathematics and computer science are provided. Subsequently, two possible paths are distinguished:
- the Computer Science and Technology path, with two orientations, one of a methodological nature, intended for those who wish to continue their studies with a Master's Degree in Computer Science and Technology, and a professionalizing orientation, intended for those who wish to complete their studies at the end of the Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science.

- the Interdisciplinary path, intended for those who wish to complete their computer science training with other complementary disciplines in biology, economics and mathematics and continue their studies in other disciplines such as a Master's Degree in Medical Biotechnology, a Master's Degree in Finance, and a Master's Degree in Mathematical Sciences. Knowledge required for access Students with a high school diploma or other equivalent qualification obtained abroad are admitted to the degree course. The necessary requirements to start studying regularly are the habit of reasoning rigorously, familiarity with mathematical language, and an interest in addressing and analyzing complex problems and in determining strategies and methods for their solution. No detailed computer skills are required, nor is knowledge of the English language necessary, as the course offers all the opportunities to learn it. Even students with a humanistic background often demonstrate success in their studies and career that is absolutely comparable to that of students with an initial technical background.

The possibility of enrolling is conditional on passing a mandatory orientation and self-assessment test. The test adopted is the CISIA national test promoted and managed by the Interuniversity Consortium of Integrated Systems for Access (hereinafter CISIA), to which the University of Trento adheres, which is delivered both on an IT platform (CISIA Online Test) and in paper form. The candidate who obtains a score of more than 20 for the paper version and 15 for the online version will be able to enroll without any outstanding requirements. For the paper version, the possibility of enrolling with outstanding requirements is provided for the candidate who obtains a score between 15 and 20. Further information is available on the website http://disi.unitn.it/test_ammissione_laurea_triennale_informatica. Verification of required knowledge for access: No. Program, texts and objectives: Specific training objectives of the course and description of the educational path. The course aims to train graduates who have a solid knowledge of various areas of mathematics (algebra, analysis, geometry, probability, numerical analysis, mathematical physics), and a more in-depth knowledge in at least one specific area. This knowledge is usually accompanied by an operational familiarity with at least one other discipline.

These skills, in addition to being based on solid theoretical foundations, also include the ability to:
- solve non-routine mathematical problems, knowing how to draw on their own cultural background to use the most appropriate tools;
- carry out complex bibliographic research, in order to be able to identify useful tools in the literature, even recent ones, for solving given problems;
- present mathematical topics effectively, also in English, adapting the presentation to different types of audiences, even non-specialized ones. Through the thesis, the student is finally guided to move autonomously and creatively in a specific area. The entire Master's Degree course is taught in English. The didactic regulations of the Master's Degree course provide for paths aimed more at a broad mathematical cultural training and paths intended to allow the graduate to understand the language, methods, and characteristics of a non-mathematical discipline, together with its relationship with mathematics itself. With this training, the graduate will be able to work more effectively in multidisciplinary working groups, making a significant contribution to modeling and solving complex problems.

- are able to operate in interdisciplinary working groups and know how to use the most appropriate communication and storytelling methods to present empirical evidence in the most suitable form to support the tactical and strategic decisions of management, paying particular attention to the issues related to the synthesis and effective representation and visualization of information; they are able to use fluently, in written and oral form, English as well as Italian, with reference also to disciplinary lexicons.

Students receive a basic sociological education enriched by the contribution of the main disciplines of the humanities and social sciences (anthropology, political science, history, psychology, economics, law, statistics), training in the methods and techniques of the main empirical research approaches, and more in-depth training in some special sociologies. The underlying objective of the degree program is to offer students, through a gradual and linear educational path, a series of tools that enable them to conduct analyses and interpretations of social reality. During the three-year period, students are presented with the concepts and theories of classical and contemporary sociological theory, with a strong focus on their applicability in an analytical key. At the same time, students in the degree program learn the methods and techniques of social research and statistics, putting the knowledge acquired into practice through concrete research experiences.

After a solid common basic education, the study plan develops according to the path chosen as most appropriate by the students. This allows the development of specific skills in graduates necessary to operate effectively in one of the following professional areas: promotion of community development and collective action with a view to environmental and social sustainability; management of organizational innovation and promotion of social entrepreneurship; conducting socio-economic and demographic descriptive and explanatory research, promotion and intervention in the field of cultural production and communication. [0620G] INTERNATIONAL STUDIES Bachelor's Degree
COURSE INFORMATION General information relating to the current academic year. Duration: 3 years. Program: 2015. Status: Open. Credits: 180 ECTS. Type: Three-year Bachelor's Degree. Category: Sociology and International Studies. Regulations: Reform 270/04. Degree Class: L-36 - Class of Degrees in Political Science and International Relations. Inter-University Course: No. Limited Access (20 places). Location: City Campus - Sociology - via Verdi, 26. Department: Department of Sociology and Social Research. Verification of knowledge required for access: No. Program, texts and objectives: Specific learning objectives of the course and description of the educational path. The main educational objective of the course is to enable students to understand the complexity of the phenomena that affect contemporary societies, studying them from different disciplinary perspectives. The perspective used is that of the transformations induced by globalization, internationalization, and Europeanization on national social, political, and economic systems.

UNIVERSITY: University of Trento

induced by globalization, internationalization, and Europeanization on national social, political, and economic systems.
Since its inception, the Bachelor's Degree in International Studies has been based on the awareness that a full understanding of these phenomena can only come from a multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary approach. The processes of globalization and internationalization of national societies raise new questions for the social sciences, making the need for interconnection and dialogue between economic, legal, political, sociological, and historical disciplines increasingly evident. This approach is reinforced and enhanced in the new curriculum. The Bachelor's Degree course can be structured into paths that differ in the professional and educational profiles that are intended to be pursued. Although sharing a multidisciplinary approach, the courses offered in the two paths can address themes that are both complementary and distinct. The Bachelor's Degree course is structured over three years. During the first year, students must learn the "fundamentals" of the main social sciences and statistics. In the field of sociology, the main concepts and notions necessary for the analysis of the configuration of society and social change are introduced.

e main concepts and notions necessary for the analysis of the configuration of society and social change are introduced.
In the field of modern and contemporary history, the main events and developments of the modern and contemporary world and their most important interpretations are presented. In the field of political science, the language and conceptualizations specific to the discipline and the analysis of the democratic process are introduced. In the field of economics, particular attention is paid to the main macroeconomic theories. In the field of public law, elements of European public law are introduced, understood as the combination of national and supranational public law. In the field of statistics, the first rudiments relating to data analysis are presented. Great importance is also given to knowledge of the English language. During the second year, the essential tools of empirical research in the field of social sciences and knowledge of international law are presented. The political systems are also presented in a comparative key, as well as their behavior and their relations within the international system.

In the historical field, the history of the modern state is analyzed, as a historically determined form of organization of power, in the European-Western context, from its medieval origins to the consolidation of the modern age, ending with some references to the crisis of the contemporary state in the face of globalization processes. As in the first year, a specialist English course completes the language offering. Some courses may be specific to the educational paths. Finally, during the third year, courses are offered that focus on more specific issues. These are dedicated to the main research topics in the field of European and international studies, the issues of social inequalities, social movements and European civil society, the issues of citizenship and European democracy, conflict management and others. A course in international economic policy completes the multidisciplinary training. By the end of the third year, students must also demonstrate knowledge of a second foreign language. To complete the educational path, some credit seminars are activated on particularly relevant topics concerning the transformation of contemporary economic, political and social systems.

Knowledge required for access: Before accessing the Bachelor's Degree course, students must possess the following skills:
a) analytical skills:
among the different types of analytical skills, the following are considered particularly important: the ability to reason logically; for example, they must be able to understand structured sets of relationships, to deduce new information from them, to analyze and evaluate arguments, to draw precise and accurate inferences, and to identify possible causal explanations, etc. b) verbal skills:
among the various types of verbal skills, the course considers the following two to be most effective in determining the quality of the study path:
- ability in understanding texts: for example, they must be able to isolate the various passages in which a fact is presented, exemplified, developed; to establish logical connections between the various passages; to synthesize the information provided by the text; etc. - ability in lexical understanding: for example, they must be able to identify analogies between terms in the lexicon, to identify the opposite of a given term, etc.

The Global and Local Studies (Glocal Studies) degree program aims to train professionals capable of designing and guiding public policies and development interventions by combining the analysis of the specific characteristics of the local contexts to which they are addressed with the analysis of the global processes that affect them.

Graduates will be able to analyze the local context in a rigorous manner in light of the changes induced by global dynamics, manage participatory processes aimed at producing public policy decisions, interact with multi-level decision-making processes and institutions, and provide local actors with the complex set of knowledge relating to development opportunities. More specifically, the graduate will be a professional: a) an expert and consultant in public policies operating in the context of local, national and international organizations, whether governmental or non-governmental; b) a consultant for territorial projects, with analytical skills applicable in the design and implementation of development and governance interventions in local contexts. In general, the degree program prepares students to analyze and intervene in specific territorial areas and on different scales, with an understanding of the global processes that affect them.

The term "Glocal," which has been adopted and consolidated in the language of social, political and territorial studies for several decades, refers to those processes that intersect, concretize and locally characterize the dynamics of globalization, and as such constitute a particular object of study for the degree program. The degree program is characterized by a strongly multidisciplinary approach and is based on political, sociological, historical, economic and legal-institutional studies. During the first year, students will acquire: - skills in quantitative and qualitative research methodology that will enable them to conduct empirical research, whether based on primary or secondary data.

In particular, the objective of the course is to enable students to acquire the theoretical knowledge and advanced methodological skills in the field of psychological disciplines necessary for application in the various contexts of professional action in psychology. The educational path is based on a solid preparation in the various disciplinary areas, ranging from clinical psychology to neuropsychology, to social and organizational psychology, with particular attention to the neurobiological basis of mental phenomena, to methodological and research aspects, and to psychological and psychosocial intervention. The student will consolidate their specialized knowledge of cognitive, affective and social processes, their biological basis and their development, as well as operational skills on the most advanced study methods of these functions and on the main techniques of habilitation and rehabilitation. The student will also acquire the most advanced methodological skills in the diagnostic field to promote the understanding of the different intervention models.

In order to pass the PPV, the student must obtain a positive assessment, following which he/she will be admitted to the discussion of the degree thesis. Those who obtain a positive assessment of the Practical-Evaluative Internship (PEI) within the courses of study are admitted to the final examination. Within the professionalizing educational activities, 20 university educational credits (CFU) are acquired through the carrying out of a PEI, within the courses of study. The PEI consists of contextualized and supervised practical activities, which provide for direct observation and the carrying out of activities aimed at situated learning and the development of the procedural and relational skills essential for the exercise of the professional activity.

These professionals meet the needs of the labor market, which often does not require specialization limited to a single sector, but rather a comprehensive understanding of the systems, methodologies and technologies of the entire information area, as well as the ability to understand the relationships between the various disciplines and to deal with interdisciplinary problems professionally. The areas of learning involved in achieving the learning objectives are:
- the area of mathematical and physical disciplines to provide basic mathematical and physical knowledge necessary to correctly apply the scientific and experimental method in problem solving;
- the area of computer science disciplines to offer solid skills in computer programming and data structure management;

- specialization courses for the acquisition of more professional skills.

COURSE STRUCTURE The Course of Studies provides a basic training, common to all engineering degrees, followed by a broad engineering training in the area of information engineering. Subsequently, the Course of Studies is structured in paths in which the student, at his own choice, will acquire specific and in-depth training in one of the areas that characterize information engineering, such as computer engineering, telecommunications engineering or electronic engineering. In order to allow the student to acquire and integrate the various knowledge required in a harmonious and balanced way, the educational offer is structured in:
1) a basic training in which both the methodological-operational aspects of mathematics and the fundamental knowledge and methodological aspects of the basic sciences of interest for information technologies are dealt with;
2) a broad engineering training in the area of information engineering, in which the fundamental contents of the disciplines that characterize the information area (electronics, computer science and telecommunications) and the knowledge of the related methodologies are acquired.

At the end of the training course, the graduate must be able to:
- Manage independently and responsibly the activities of prevention, verification and control on the quality of living and working environments
- Manage the methods of sampling and analysis of air, water, soil and food data and biological matrices for the purpose of prevention in both living and working environments;
- define the priorities of interventions based on health and safety needs, organizational needs and the optimal use of available resources;
- design, implement and deliver, in collaboration with other professionals, information and educational interventions for the control and prevention of risk factors aimed at individuals and groups;
- Use tools and methodologies for the evaluation and review of professional, organizational and relational quality;
- Manage prevention and control interventions to ensure the safety and health of food and beverages intended for consumption from the production phase to consumption
- Identify, analyze and evaluate the risks to safety and health (plants and equipment, physical, chemical, biological agents, psychosocial, organizational and ergonomic factors) and identify the most effective and appropriate prevention techniques and measures for the problem identified.

The prerequisites required for the student who wishes to enroll in the course should include:
